packs.label: Merixa Management Reporting Technical Method Notes

terms.title: Working paper discipline and source control
terms.definition:
Use for every Management Reporting task before analysis starts. Controlled working paper file. 1. Save original source files unchanged.
2. Create a separate working copy and record every transformation.
3. Use MR step references in file names and workpaper headings.
4. Record source owner, extraction date, period and whether the file is draft or final.
5. Cross-reference final outputs back to working papers.
terms.example: 1. Save original source files unchanged. 2. Create a separate working copy and record every transformation. 3. Use MR step references in file names and workpaper headings. 4. Record source owner, extraction date, period and whether the file is draft or final. 5. Cross-reference final outputs back to working papers.
terms.commonError:
• Data received through unapproved channels.
• Unexplained manual changes to client data.
• Unsupported assumptions embedded in formulas.
terms.formula: No formula. Control rule: no source owner + no extraction date + no reconciliation = not ready for conclusion.
terms.howToUse:
• Every source file has provenance.
• Every output has a working paper reference.
• Every assumption has an owner and date.
terms.components: SoW, source files, data request tracker, query log, issue log, assumptions register, version control sheet.

terms.title: Reconciliation and cut-off control
terms.definition: Use before analysing management accounts, trends, margins, cash or forecasts. Reconciliation sheet and difference log.
terms.example: 1. Agree the period and cut-off date. 2. Tie management pack totals to the trial balance or ledger control totals. 3. Tie sub-ledgers to ledger control accounts. 4. Investigate differences and classify them as timing, reclassification, error, manual adjustment or unexplained. 5. Do not issue analysis on unreconciled material numbers.
terms.commonError:
• Management pack cannot be reconciled to TB.
• Material unposted journals.
• Unclear cut-off on sales, purchases, payroll or inventory.
terms.formula: Difference = Source A total - Source B total. Difference % = Difference / Source B total.
terms.howToUse:
• Totals agree or differences are explained.
• Comparatives are on the same basis.
• Draft figures are labelled as draft.
terms.components: Trial balance, management accounts, nominal ledger, prior pack, bank/cash records, relevant sub-ledgers.

terms.title: Revenue bridge and price-volume-mix logic
terms.definition: Use when explaining revenue movement between periods, budget, forecast or scenarios. Revenue bridge chart, table and commentary.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile total revenue to management accounts. 2. Select bridge dimensions supported by the data. 3. Separate price, volume and mix only where unit and product data are reliable. 4. Identify one-off revenue, timing and discontinued/new activity. 5. Prepare bridge table and explanatory narrative.
terms.commonError:
• Missing quantity data.
• Changing product definitions.
• One-off invoices masking recurring trend.
terms.formula: Revenue movement = Current revenue - Comparative revenue. Price effect = (Current price - Prior price) x Current or prior volume (chosen method must be documented). Volume effect = (Current volume - Prior volume) x Prior price. Mix effect = residual where product mix changed and data supports calculation.
terms.howToUse:
• Bridge total equals total revenue movement.
• Credit notes/rebates are treated consistently.
• Residual or unexplained movement is labelled.
terms.components: Sales by product/customer/site/channel, quantity/volume, unit price, credit notes/rebates, prior period, budget/forecast.

terms.title: Credit notes, rebates and revenue leakage
terms.definition: Use when deductions reduce revenue or margin and require management visibility. Revenue leakage analysis and issue log.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile deductions to contra-revenue or credit note accounts. 2. Analyse by customer, product, reason code and period. 3. Identify recurring deductions and exceptional claims. 4. Quantify margin effect where cost data is available. 5. Route weak approval or dispute controls to Risk & Control if required.
terms.commonError:
• Large manual credit notes near period end.
• Undefined rebate agreements.
• Missing approval trail.
terms.formula: Net revenue = Gross revenue - credit notes - rebates - discounts - claims. Leakage % = deductions / gross revenue.
terms.howToUse:
• Deductions reconcile to ledger.
• Reason codes are meaningful.
• Claims are not double counted.
terms.components: Credit note listing, rebate agreements, customer claims, sales ledger, revenue ledger, approval evidence.

terms.title: Margin analysis: gross, contribution and net margin
terms.definition: Use to explain profitability at company, product, customer, site or channel level. Margin bridge and commentary.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile revenue and cost bases to management accounts. 2. Define which margin measure is being used. 3. Calculate margin by relevant dimension only where data is reliable. 4. Investigate movement by price, volume, mix, cost rate, usage and allocation changes. 5. Explain limitations where costs are allocated rather than directly traced.
terms.commonError:
• Negative margins caused by miscoding.
• Unallocated costs omitted.
• Allocated overhead presented as directly caused.
terms.formula: Gross margin = Revenue - Cost of sales. Gross margin % = Gross margin / Revenue. Contribution = Revenue - Variable costs. Contribution margin % = Contribution / Revenue. Net margin = Revenue - Direct costs - allocated overheads.
terms.howToUse:
• Cost classifications are consistent.
• Allocation bases are documented.
• Margins are not compared where definitions differ.
terms.components: Revenue, cost of sales, variable costs, direct costs, allocated overheads, operating expenses, allocation basis.

terms.title: Cost classification
terms.definition: Use when ledger structure does not produce meaningful management reporting. Cost classification matrix.
terms.example: 1. Classify costs by nature, function, behaviour and controllability. 2. Identify miscoded, inconsistent or ambiguous accounts. 3. Propose management reporting reclassifications without changing statutory records unless separately authorised. 4. Document logic and effect by line item. 5. Use consistent classification in all analyses.
terms.commonError:
• Costs classified to improve appearance rather than truth.
• Statutory treatment confused with management classification.
terms.formula: Common classes: direct/indirect, fixed/variable/semi-variable, controllable/uncontrollable, product/period, recurring/non-recurring.
terms.howToUse:
• Classifications are consistent with purpose.
• Significant reclassifications are quantified.
• Client confirms disputed classifications.
terms.components: Chart of accounts, nominal ledger, cost centre list, management reporting dimensions, client coding rules.

terms.title: Cost allocation basis review
terms.definition: Use when costs are allocated to products, sites, customers, projects or departments. Allocation basis memo and recalculation.
terms.example: 1. List cost pools and current allocation bases. 2. Assess whether each basis is causal, consistent, practical and understandable. 3. Test alternative bases for material cost pools. 4. Quantify financial effect of changing allocation. 5. Recommend basis only where it improves decision usefulness.
terms.commonError:
• Allocation basis chosen to manipulate performance.
• Driver data unavailable.
• Central costs over-allocated to weak units.
terms.formula: Allocated cost = Cost pool x (recipient driver units / total driver units).
terms.howToUse:
• Driver totals agree.
• No recipient receives cost without rationale.
• Changes are not made without comparatives.
terms.components: Current allocation model, cost pools, allocation drivers, volume/activity data, cost centre structure.

terms.title: Cost-driver identification
terms.definition:
Use when explaining why costs move or designing driver-based forecasts. Cost-driver map. 1. Select material cost categories.
2. Interview owners to identify activities causing cost.
3. Compare cost movement to activity movement.
4. Separate accounting allocation drivers from operational cost drivers.
5. Document driver confidence level.
terms.example: 1. Select material cost categories. 2. Interview owners to identify activities causing cost. 3. Compare cost movement to activity movement. 4. Separate accounting allocation drivers from operational cost drivers. 5. Document driver confidence level.
terms.commonError:
• Correlation mistaken for causation.
• Using revenue as default driver for unrelated costs.
terms.formula: Cost per driver unit = Cost / Driver units. Driver effect = Change in driver units x Cost per driver unit.
terms.howToUse:
• Driver relationship is plausible.
• Outliers are investigated.
• Driver is controllable or observable.
terms.components: Cost history, activity data, process owner interviews, operational KPIs.

terms.title: Operating expense analysis
terms.definition: Use for overhead review, departmental reporting and management commentary. Opex analysis table and commentary.
terms.example: 1. Group expenses into meaningful categories. 2. Compare actual vs prior, budget and forecast. 3. Identify run-rate, timing, one-off, seasonal and step-change items. 4. Investigate material movements with ledger detail. 5. Prepare commentary by driver and action.
terms.commonError:
• Large unexplained accruals/reversals.
• Personal or unusual expenditure.
• Missing supplier detail.
terms.formula: Variance = Actual - Comparator. Run-rate = recurring monthly cost x 12 or relevant period.
terms.howToUse:
• Outliers are explained.
• One-offs are supported.
• Cost categories are consistent.
terms.components: Operating expense ledger, budget/forecast, prior periods, contracts, headcount, operational context.

terms.title: Payroll and staff cost bridge
terms.definition:
Use for staffing cost movement, departmental cost or forecast analysis. Payroll bridge. 1. Reconcile payroll to ledger.
2. Split movement by headcount, rate, mix, overtime, bonus, contractor and one-off effects.
3. Check department coding and capitalised/project treatment where relevant.
4. Compare payroll movement to operational capacity or revenue where useful.
5. Document sensitivity to hiring assumptions.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile payroll to ledger. 2. Split movement by headcount, rate, mix, overtime, bonus, contractor and one-off effects. 3. Check department coding and capitalised/project treatment where relevant. 4. Compare payroll movement to operational capacity or revenue where useful. 5. Document sensitivity to hiring assumptions.
terms.commonError:
• HR/legal matters.
• Unexplained capitalisation.
• Confidential salary data handling.
terms.formula: Average cost per FTE = Payroll cost / average FTE. Headcount effect = change in FTE x prior average cost. Rate effect = current FTE x change in average rate.
terms.howToUse:
• FTE definitions are consistent.
• Bonus/one-off amounts are separated.
• Payroll agrees to ledger.
terms.components: Payroll summary, headcount, starters/leavers, salary rates, overtime, bonus, contractor costs, ledger payroll accounts.

terms.title: Divisional, site, project and contract profitability
terms.definition:
Use for decentralised performance reporting. Dimension profitability pack. 1. Confirm hierarchy and ownership.
2. Reconcile dimension totals to overall accounts.
3. Separate direct costs from allocated costs.
4. Calculate relevant margins and KPIs.
5. Interpret performance with operational context and allocation caveats.
terms.example: 1. Confirm hierarchy and ownership. 2. Reconcile dimension totals to overall accounts. 3. Separate direct costs from allocated costs. 4. Calculate relevant margins and KPIs. 5. Interpret performance with operational context and allocation caveats.
terms.commonError:
• Incomplete coding.
• Cost allocations driving false conclusions.
• Contractual/legal issues.
terms.formula: Segment margin = Segment revenue - directly attributable costs - supportable allocated costs.
terms.howToUse:
• Unallocated costs are visible.
• Coding completeness checked.
• Comparatives on same basis.
terms.components: Dimension-level revenue/cost, cost centres, project ledgers, site data, allocation bases, operational measures.

terms.title: Trend analysis and one-off separation
terms.definition:
Use for multi-period movement and abnormal item analysis. Trend analysis and one-off schedule. 1. Select comparable periods.
2. Calculate absolute, percentage and common-size movements.
3. Identify seasonality, trend, step-change and one-off items.
4. Separate reported and adjusted management views.
5. Explain reason and implication.
terms.example: 1. Select comparable periods. 2. Calculate absolute, percentage and common-size movements. 3. Identify seasonality, trend, step-change and one-off items. 4. Separate reported and adjusted management views. 5. Explain reason and implication.
terms.commonError:
• Rebasing comparatives without disclosure.
• Calling recurring losses one-off.
terms.formula: Change % = (Current - Comparative) / Comparative. Common-size ratio = line item / relevant total.
terms.howToUse:
• Periods are comparable.
• One-offs are evidenced.
• Adjusted views are labelled.
terms.components: Monthly/quarterly data, prior periods, budget/forecast, ledger detail, operational events.

terms.title: Variance analysis
terms.definition: Use for actual vs budget, actual vs forecast, prior-period and standard cost comparisons. Variance report.
terms.example: 1. Confirm comparison base. 2. Calculate value and percentage variance. 3. Apply materiality threshold. 4. Analyse drivers: price, volume, mix, rate, efficiency, timing and allocation. 5. Record explanation, owner and action.
terms.commonError:
• Using budget errors as operating explanations.
• No owner for action.
terms.formula: Variance = Actual - Comparator. Sales price variance = (Actual price - Standard price) x Actual volume. Volume variance = (Actual volume - Standard volume) x Standard margin or price.
terms.howToUse:
• Comparator is approved.
• Favourable/adverse signs are clear.
• Explanations are evidenced.
terms.components: Actuals, budget/forecast/standard, assumptions, ledger detail, operational drivers.

terms.title: Financial-operational bridging
terms.definition:
Use to connect financial results with business events. Finance-to-operations bridge. 1. Select material financial movements.
2. Identify operational events that should explain them.
3. Align timing and definitions.
4. Quantify the link where possible.
5. Document gaps between operational and financial views.
terms.example: 1. Select material financial movements. 2. Identify operational events that should explain them. 3. Align timing and definitions. 4. Quantify the link where possible. 5. Document gaps between operational and financial views.
terms.commonError:
• Operational KPIs not reconciled.
• Different definitions between teams.
terms.formula: Example: Revenue movement linked to orders x average order value x conversion/fulfilment rate.
terms.howToUse:
• Timing differences are understood.
• Operational KPI definitions are checked.
• Unexplained gaps logged.
terms.components: Financial results, operational KPIs, volume/activity data, production/service/customer/site information.

terms.title: Management commentary standard
terms.definition:
Use for all client-facing commentary. Clear management commentary. 1. Write one point per material issue.
2. Use the structure: what happened, why, impact, action/owner.
3. Distinguish fact from interpretation.
4. Add limitations where data is provisional or incomplete.
5. Remove unsupported claims and excessive language.
terms.example: 1. Write one point per material issue. 2. Use the structure: what happened, why, impact, action/owner. 3. Distinguish fact from interpretation. 4. Add limitations where data is provisional or incomplete. 5. Remove unsupported claims and excessive language.
terms.commonError:
• Conclusions from unreconciled data.
• Guarantees or legal/tax advice.
terms.formula: Commentary sentence model: “Based on [source], [metric] moved by [amount] mainly due to [driver]. Management should consider [action], subject to [limitation].”
terms.howToUse:
• Commentary ties to numbers.
• No audit/assurance wording.
• No blame or legal conclusion.
terms.components: Reconciled analysis, issue log, assumptions, client explanations, action tracker.

terms.title: Management pack summary page
terms.definition:
Use to create executive-level visibility. Executive summary page. 1. Select only material messages.
2. Show performance, cash, forward view and actions.
3. Use clear headings and consistent definitions.
4. Include limitations and data status where necessary.
5. Cross-check all numbers to source schedules.
terms.example: 1. Select only material messages. 2. Show performance, cash, forward view and actions. 3. Use clear headings and consistent definitions. 4. Include limitations and data status where necessary. 5. Cross-check all numbers to source schedules.
terms.commonError:
• Too many metrics.
• Unsupported “red/amber/green” status.
terms.formula: No formula. Summary logic: result + driver + implication + action.
terms.howToUse:
• No contradiction with detail pages.
• Every number is sourced.
• Action owners included.
terms.components: Final analysis, KPI status, cash position, key variances, actions, risks and assumptions.

terms.title: Model integrity testing
terms.definition:
Use for budgets, forecasts, cash forecasts and business cases. Model integrity checklist. 1. Create a backup copy.
2. Check formulas, hardcodes, hidden sheets, external links and circular references.
3. Trace key outputs back to inputs.
4. Test signs, dates, units, blank rows and totals.
5. Document model risks and fixes.
terms.example: 1. Create a backup copy. 2. Check formulas, hardcodes, hidden sheets, external links and circular references. 3. Trace key outputs back to inputs. 4. Test signs, dates, units, blank rows and totals. 5. Document model risks and fixes.
terms.commonError:
• Unprotected formulas.
• Hardcoded outputs.
• Uncontrolled versions.
terms.formula: Formula checks: cross-casts, vertical totals, balance checks, control accounts, reasonableness checks.
terms.howToUse:
• Outputs equal supporting schedules.
• Input cells separated from formulas.
• External links controlled.
terms.components: Excel model, source data, assumptions, output sheets, prior versions.

terms.title: Driver-based planning structure
terms.definition:
Use for budgets and rolling forecasts. Driver-based model. 1. Define planning output and horizon.
2. Identify revenue, cost, payroll, capex and working capital drivers.
3. Build input, calculation and output sections.
4. Document each assumption and owner.
5. Test model behaviour under changes.
terms.example: 1. Define planning output and horizon. 2. Identify revenue, cost, payroll, capex and working capital drivers. 3. Build input, calculation and output sections. 4. Document each assumption and owner. 5. Test model behaviour under changes.
terms.commonError:
• Line-item budgeting without drivers.
• Unowned assumptions.
terms.formula: Financial line = activity driver x rate x timing factor, or fixed schedule where no driver applies.
terms.howToUse:
• Drivers are observable.
• Assumptions are owner-approved.
• Outputs reconcile to baseline.
terms.components: Actuals, business drivers, planning assumptions, owner submissions, operational plans.

terms.title: Revenue forecasting
terms.definition:
Use for revenue budget, forecast or scenario model. Revenue forecast schedule. 1. Reconcile baseline to actual revenue.
2. Split revenue into recurring, new, one-off and discontinued streams.
3. Apply volume, price, conversion, renewal and timing assumptions.
4. Compare forecast to run-rate and known events.
5. Document confidence and sensitivity.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile baseline to actual revenue. 2. Split revenue into recurring, new, one-off and discontinued streams. 3. Apply volume, price, conversion, renewal and timing assumptions. 4. Compare forecast to run-rate and known events. 5. Document confidence and sensitivity.
terms.commonError:
• Unsupported growth assumptions.
• Pipeline treated as contracted.
terms.formula: Forecast revenue = volume/customers x price x conversion/retention x timing factor.
terms.howToUse:
• Pipeline not double counted.
• One-offs separated.
• Seasonality considered.
terms.components: Historical revenue, pipeline, contracts, customer data, price lists, churn/retention, volume indicators.

terms.title: Cost forecasting
terms.definition:
Use for opex, cost of sales or departmental forecasts. Cost forecast schedule. 1. Classify costs by behaviour and commitment.
2. Reconcile baseline to actuals.
3. Apply driver, contract, run-rate or event-based logic.
4. Phase costs by expected timing.
5. Document assumptions and risks.
terms.example: 1. Classify costs by behaviour and commitment. 2. Reconcile baseline to actuals. 3. Apply driver, contract, run-rate or event-based logic. 4. Phase costs by expected timing. 5. Document assumptions and risks.
terms.commonError: • Costs forecast as simple percentage of revenue without rationale.
terms.formula: Forecast cost = fixed cost schedule + variable cost per unit x forecast activity + known step costs.
terms.howToUse:
• Committed costs included.
• One-offs treated separately.
• Inflation assumptions visible.
terms.components: Historic cost, contracts, suppliers, volumes, inflation, headcount, business plans.

terms.title: Payroll forecasting
terms.definition:
Use for headcount and staff cost planning. Payroll forecast. 1. Reconcile payroll baseline to actuals.
2. Build forecast by role or group.
3. Add start dates, salary rates, employer costs, bonus/overtime and leavers.
4. Check phasing and vacancies.
5. Document HR-provided assumptions.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile payroll baseline to actuals. 2. Build forecast by role or group. 3. Add start dates, salary rates, employer costs, bonus/overtime and leavers. 4. Check phasing and vacancies. 5. Document HR-provided assumptions.
terms.commonError:
• Personal data exposure.
• Legal/HR advice.
terms.formula: Payroll forecast = sum(FTE x salary rate x months employed) + employer costs + bonus/overtime/contractors.
terms.howToUse:
• Start dates correct.
• Employer costs included.
• Confidentiality protected.
terms.components: Headcount plan, salary data, payroll actuals, starters/leavers, bonus, benefits, employer costs.

terms.title: Capex and project spend forecast
terms.definition:
Use for investment, project, equipment or system spend forecasting. Capex forecast. 1. Separate capex from operating cost.
2. Confirm approval status and committed/uncommitted spend.
3. Phase spend by milestone and payment terms.
4. Separate P&L depreciation from cash outflow where needed.
5. Route valuation/tax/accounting policy issues out of scope.
terms.example: 1. Separate capex from operating cost. 2. Confirm approval status and committed/uncommitted spend. 3. Phase spend by milestone and payment terms. 4. Separate P&L depreciation from cash outflow where needed. 5. Route valuation/tax/accounting policy issues out of scope.
terms.commonError:
• Tax relief advice requested.
• Investment recommendation requested.
terms.formula: Cash capex = expected invoice/payment timing. P&L effect may include depreciation separately if requested.
terms.howToUse:
• Approvals confirmed.
• Cash vs P&L distinguished.
• Projects not duplicated.
terms.components: Capex plan, project budgets, purchase orders, supplier quotes, depreciation if in scope, cash timing.

terms.title: Working capital forecast assumptions
terms.definition:
Use for balance sheet and cash forecasts. Working capital assumption schedule. 1. Calculate historic working capital days.
2. Agree future receipt, payment and inventory assumptions.
3. Translate assumptions into cash timing and balance movement.
4. Stress test assumptions when cash is tight.
5. Document assumptions by owner.
terms.example: 1. Calculate historic working capital days. 2. Agree future receipt, payment and inventory assumptions. 3. Translate assumptions into cash timing and balance movement. 4. Stress test assumptions when cash is tight. 5. Document assumptions by owner.
terms.commonError: • Assumed collection improvement without action plan.
terms.formula: DSO = Trade receivables / credit sales x days. DPO = Trade payables / purchases or cost of sales x days. DIO = Inventory / cost of sales x days.
terms.howToUse:
• Definitions consistent.
• Terms and behaviour considered.
• Assumptions linked to cash forecast.
terms.components: AR/AP/inventory ageing, payment terms, sales forecast, purchasing forecast, historic DSO/DPO/DIO.

terms.title: Actual vs budget/forecast analysis
terms.definition:
Use for performance review and planning feedback. Variance analysis pack. 1. Reconcile actuals.
2. Use approved comparator.
3. Calculate variance and percentage movement.
4. Explain with business drivers.
5. Record actions and owners.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile actuals. 2. Use approved comparator. 3. Calculate variance and percentage movement. 4. Explain with business drivers. 5. Record actions and owners.
terms.commonError: • Explaining variances only as “phasing” without evidence.
terms.formula: Variance = Actual - Budget/Forecast. Variance % = Variance / Budget/Forecast.
terms.howToUse:
• Comparator version controlled.
• Material thresholds applied.
• Explanations evidenced.
terms.components: Actuals, approved budget, latest forecast, ledger, operational data.

terms.title: Forecast accuracy review
terms.definition:
Use to improve forecasting discipline. Forecast accuracy report. 1. Compare forecast made at a point in time to actual outcome.
2. Calculate error by line item, owner and period.
3. Identify bias, timing error and assumption error.
4. Update assumptions and process recommendations.
5. Do not blame individuals; focus on process improvement.
terms.example: 1. Compare forecast made at a point in time to actual outcome. 2. Calculate error by line item, owner and period. 3. Identify bias, timing error and assumption error. 4. Update assumptions and process recommendations. 5. Do not blame individuals; focus on process improvement.
terms.commonError:
• Overwriting old forecasts.
• Penalising reasonable uncertainty.
terms.formula: Forecast error = Actual - Forecast. Error % = Error / Forecast. Accuracy % = 1 - absolute(error) / actual or forecast (definition must be documented).
terms.howToUse:
• Forecast versions are dated.
• Changes after issue are excluded from original accuracy test.
terms.components: Prior forecasts, actual results, forecast dates, assumptions, owner submissions.

terms.title: Forecast bridge
terms.definition:
Use to explain movement from prior forecast to latest forecast. Forecast bridge. 1. Lock prior forecast version.
2. Reconcile both forecast totals.
3. Identify changes in volume, price, cost, timing, working capital and one-offs.
4. Separate actual performance from assumption changes.
5. Prepare bridge and commentary.
terms.example: 1. Lock prior forecast version. 2. Reconcile both forecast totals. 3. Identify changes in volume, price, cost, timing, working capital and one-offs. 4. Separate actual performance from assumption changes. 5. Prepare bridge and commentary.
terms.commonError: • Reforecasting without explaining change.
terms.formula: Forecast movement = Latest forecast - Prior forecast. Split by documented drivers.
terms.howToUse:
• Prior version not overwritten.
• Drivers sum to total movement.
terms.components: Prior forecast, latest forecast, assumption changes, actuals, business events.

terms.title: Scenario analysis
terms.definition:
Use to assess alternative future states. Scenario comparison. 1. Define scenario narrative.
2. Change relevant assumptions consistently.
3. Create base, downside and upside cases if useful.
4. Compare impact on key outputs.
5. State assumptions and uncertainty clearly.
terms.example: 1. Define scenario narrative. 2. Change relevant assumptions consistently. 3. Create base, downside and upside cases if useful. 4. Compare impact on key outputs. 5. State assumptions and uncertainty clearly.
terms.commonError: • Treating scenario as prediction.
terms.formula: Scenario output = base model recalculated under alternative linked assumptions.
terms.howToUse:
• Scenario changes are controlled.
• Outputs labelled as illustrative.
terms.components: Base model, scenario assumptions, management-defined scenario narratives.

terms.title: Sensitivity analysis
terms.definition:
Use to identify variables that materially affect a conclusion. Sensitivity table. 1. Select key variables.
2. Change one variable at a time unless combined sensitivity is required.
3. Record impact on output.
4. Rank sensitivities and identify critical assumptions.
5. Use results to guide management attention.
terms.example: 1. Select key variables. 2. Change one variable at a time unless combined sensitivity is required. 3. Record impact on output. 4. Rank sensitivities and identify critical assumptions. 5. Use results to guide management attention.
terms.commonError:
• Changing multiple variables without label.
• Using arbitrary ranges.
terms.formula: Sensitivity impact = revised output - base output. Break-even sensitivity = change required for output to reach threshold.
terms.howToUse:
• Inputs changed consistently.
• Range is reasonable.
• Conclusion updated for fragile outputs.
terms.components: Model, key assumptions, output metric, threshold for concern.

terms.title: Resource allocation view
terms.definition: Use when planning resources across functions, projects, sites or products. Resource allocation matrix.
terms.example: 1. Define available resource and constraint. 2. Compare resource use to return, risk and strategic priority. 3. Rank options using agreed criteria. 4. Identify trade-offs and constraints. 5. Present for management decision.
terms.commonError: • Purely financial ranking where strategic constraints matter.
terms.formula: Return per constraint = contribution or cash benefit / constrained resource unit.
terms.howToUse:
• Criteria agreed.
• Non-financial factors included.
terms.components: Budget/forecast, capacity, headcount, margin, cash, strategic priorities.

terms.title: Cash reconciliation
terms.definition:
Use before cash analysis or cash forecasting. Cash reconciliation. 1. Reconcile bank to ledger at period end.
2. Identify reconciling items.
3. Separate restricted cash, foreign currency and overdrafts.
4. Correct or document differences.
5. Use reconciled opening cash for forecasts.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile bank to ledger at period end. 2. Identify reconciling items. 3. Separate restricted cash, foreign currency and overdrafts. 4. Correct or document differences. 5. Use reconciled opening cash for forecasts.
terms.commonError:
• Unexplained cash differences.
• Overdrafts netted without explanation.
terms.formula: Reconciled cash = bank balance + receipts in transit - unpresented payments +/- other reconciling items.
terms.howToUse:
• Bank agrees to ledger or differences explained.
• Opening cash in forecast agrees to reconciliation.
terms.components: Bank statements, bank reports, cash book, general ledger cash accounts.

terms.title: Receipts and payments history analysis
terms.definition:
Use to understand cash behaviour and forecast timing. Cash behaviour analysis. 1. Categorise historical receipts and payments.
2. Analyse timing by customer/supplier/category.
3. Identify recurring cycles and one-offs.
4. Use history to support forecast assumptions.
5. Document exceptions.
terms.example: 1. Categorise historical receipts and payments. 2. Analyse timing by customer/supplier/category. 3. Identify recurring cycles and one-offs. 4. Use history to support forecast assumptions. 5. Document exceptions.
terms.commonError:
• Unmatched bank transactions.
• Receipts assumed without collection evidence.
terms.formula: Average receipt lag = receipt date - invoice date. Average payment lag = payment date - invoice date.
terms.howToUse:
• Categories reconcile to bank movements.
• One-offs excluded from run-rate where appropriate.
terms.components: Bank transactions, AR/AP, sales/purchase ledgers, payment runs.

terms.title: Aged receivables analysis
terms.definition:
Use for debtor visibility and collections prioritisation. AR dashboard and action list. 1. Reconcile AR total to ledger.
2. Analyse by ageing bucket, customer, concentration and dispute status.
3. Calculate DSO and overdue %.
4. Identify collection priorities.
5. Separate visibility from credit control policy advice unless scoped.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile AR total to ledger. 2. Analyse by ageing bucket, customer, concentration and dispute status. 3. Calculate DSO and overdue %. 4. Identify collection priorities. 5. Separate visibility from credit control policy advice unless scoped.
terms.commonError:
• Large old balances without explanation.
• Related party balances.
terms.formula: DSO = trade receivables / credit sales x days. Overdue % = overdue receivables / total receivables.
terms.howToUse:
• Total agrees to ledger.
• Disputed balances identified.
• Credit notes considered.
terms.components: Aged receivables, sales ledger, customer list, disputes, credit notes.

terms.title: Aged payables analysis
terms.definition:
Use for supplier payment visibility and cash planning. AP analysis and payment visibility. 1. Reconcile AP to ledger.
2. Analyse by ageing, supplier, criticality and dispute status.
3. Calculate DPO where data supports it.
4. Identify overdue and priority payments.
5. Do not advise payment withholding or legal strategy.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile AP to ledger. 2. Analyse by ageing, supplier, criticality and dispute status. 3. Calculate DPO where data supports it. 4. Identify overdue and priority payments. 5. Do not advise payment withholding or legal strategy.
terms.commonError:
• Statutory/tax payments overdue.
• Supplier disputes with legal implications.
terms.formula: DPO = trade payables / purchases or cost of sales x days. Overdue % = overdue payables / total payables.
terms.howToUse:
• Supplier balances agree.
• Critical suppliers identified.
terms.components: Aged payables, purchase ledger, supplier list, payment runs, disputed invoices.

terms.title: Inventory analysis
terms.definition:
Use where inventory materially affects cash or margin. Inventory visibility report. 1. Reconcile inventory to ledger.
2. Analyse inventory days and ageing.
3. Identify slow-moving, obsolete and high-value stock.
4. Connect stock movement to sales and purchasing.
5. Route valuation policy issues to IFRS/statutory reporting if needed.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile inventory to ledger. 2. Analyse inventory days and ageing. 3. Identify slow-moving, obsolete and high-value stock. 4. Connect stock movement to sales and purchasing. 5. Route valuation policy issues to IFRS/statutory reporting if needed.
terms.commonError:
• Valuation and NRV questions.
• Physical count issues.
terms.formula: DIO = inventory / cost of sales x days. Inventory turn = cost of sales / average inventory.
terms.howToUse:
• Inventory total agrees.
• Write-downs considered.
• Definitions documented.
terms.components: Inventory listing, ageing, valuation, movements, sales data, purchasing data.

terms.title: Cash conversion cycle
terms.definition:
Use to summarise operating cash cycle. CCC dashboard. 1. Calculate DSO, DIO and DPO consistently.
2. Compute CCC.
3. Compare over time and to target where available.
4. Explain movement by component.
5. Avoid overinterpreting a single period-end number.
terms.example: 1. Calculate DSO, DIO and DPO consistently. 2. Compute CCC. 3. Compare over time and to target where available. 4. Explain movement by component. 5. Avoid overinterpreting a single period-end number.
terms.commonError: • Negative or unusual CCC not explained.
terms.formula: CCC = DSO + DIO - DPO.
terms.howToUse:
• Definitions consistent.
• Averages used where period-end distortion exists.
terms.components: DSO, DIO, DPO calculations and underlying balances.

terms.title: Cash tied in operations
terms.definition:
Use to identify liquidity absorbed by operations. Cash tied in operations analysis. 1. Calculate movement in operating working capital.
2. Identify cash absorbed/released by AR, inventory and AP.
3. Prioritise material drivers.
4. Link to operational causes and actions.
5. Document assumptions.
terms.example: 1. Calculate movement in operating working capital. 2. Identify cash absorbed/released by AR, inventory and AP. 3. Prioritise material drivers. 4. Link to operational causes and actions. 5. Document assumptions.
terms.commonError: • Ignoring VAT/tax timing or other operating balances.
terms.formula: Cash tied in WC = increase in AR + increase in inventory - increase in AP, adjusted for other operating balances as defined.
terms.howToUse:
• Opening/closing balances reconcile.
• Movement agrees to cash flow view where relevant.
terms.components: AR/AP/inventory movements, working capital bridge, sales/cost data.

terms.title: week cash forecasting
terms.definition:
Use for short-term liquidity visibility. 13-week cash forecast. 1. Set weekly columns and reconcile opening cash.
2. Forecast receipts from debtor ageing and expected sales.
3. Forecast payments from AP, payroll, tax and recurring commitments.
4. Calculate weekly net movement and closing cash.
5. Update actuals weekly and review variance.
terms.example: 1. Set weekly columns and reconcile opening cash. 2. Forecast receipts from debtor ageing and expected sales. 3. Forecast payments from AP, payroll, tax and recurring commitments. 4. Calculate weekly net movement and closing cash. 5. Update actuals weekly and review variance.
terms.commonError:
• Going concern/covenant triggers.
• Unconfirmed facility access.
terms.formula: Closing cash = Opening cash + receipts - payments. Minimum headroom = closing cash + available facility - required minimum cash.
terms.howToUse:
• Opening cash agrees to bank.
• Tax/payroll included.
• Receipts evidence assessed.
terms.components: Opening cash, AR collections, sales pipeline, AP, payroll, tax, rent, debt, capex, other receipts/payments.

terms.title: Liquidity runway
terms.definition:
Use where cash headroom or survival period is a management concern. Liquidity runway analysis. 1. Define available liquidity.
2. Calculate base and downside cash burn.
3. Estimate runway until minimum cash threshold or facility limit.
4. Identify trigger points and actions.
5. Escalate going concern/covenant issues.
terms.example: 1. Define available liquidity. 2. Calculate base and downside cash burn. 3. Estimate runway until minimum cash threshold or facility limit. 4. Identify trigger points and actions. 5. Escalate going concern/covenant issues.
terms.commonError:
• Going concern implications.
• Debt covenant breach risk.
terms.formula: Runway = available liquidity / average net cash burn per period, subject to timing profile.
terms.howToUse:
• Facility availability confirmed.
• Burn rate excludes/ includes one-offs transparently.
terms.components: Cash forecast, facilities, committed payments, burn rate, scenario outputs.

terms.title: Working capital movement bridge
terms.definition:
Use to explain operating cash movement. Working capital bridge. 1. Reconcile balances.
2. Calculate movement by component.
3. Link movements to sales, collections, inventory build and supplier timing.
4. Quantify cash absorbed/released.
5. Prepare commentary and actions.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile balances. 2. Calculate movement by component. 3. Link movements to sales, collections, inventory build and supplier timing. 4. Quantify cash absorbed/released. 5. Prepare commentary and actions.
terms.commonError:
• Sign errors.
• Non-operating balances mixed in.
terms.formula: Cash effect: AR increase absorbs cash; inventory increase absorbs cash; AP increase releases cash.
terms.howToUse:
• Sign convention clear.
• Balances agree.
terms.components: Opening/closing AR, AP, inventory and other operating balances.

terms.title: Cash reporting dashboard
terms.definition:
Use for recurring cash visibility. Cash dashboard design. 1. Define user and cadence.
2. Select cash, forecast, ageing, runway and action metrics.
3. Design one-page layout with status, trend and actions.
4. Map each metric to source and owner.
5. Test refresh process.
terms.example: 1. Define user and cadence. 2. Select cash, forecast, ageing, runway and action metrics. 3. Design one-page layout with status, trend and actions. 4. Map each metric to source and owner. 5. Test refresh process.
terms.commonError: • Dashboard without action route.
terms.formula: Dashboard formulae depend on selected KPIs; use KPI dictionary definitions.
terms.howToUse:
• Each metric has owner/source.
• No unsupported automation assumed.
terms.components: Cash forecast, bank balances, AR/AP ageing, CCC, runway, actions.

terms.title: Cash forecast variance review
terms.definition:
Use after actual cash results are available. Cash variance report. 1. Lock original forecast.
2. Compare actual receipts and payments to forecast.
3. Split variance into timing, amount and missing item differences.
4. Update assumptions and future forecast.
5. Record owner feedback.
terms.example: 1. Lock original forecast. 2. Compare actual receipts and payments to forecast. 3. Split variance into timing, amount and missing item differences. 4. Update assumptions and future forecast. 5. Record owner feedback.
terms.commonError:
• Overwriting forecasts.
• Recurring forecast misses ignored.
terms.formula: Cash forecast variance = actual cash movement - forecast cash movement.
terms.howToUse:
• Original forecast version retained.
• Actuals reconcile to bank.
terms.components: Prior cash forecast, actual bank movements, receipts/payments detail.

terms.title: Working capital action prioritisation
terms.definition:
Use to turn working capital insight into management actions. Working capital action plan. 1. List potential actions.
2. Quantify indicative cash effect where supportable.
3. Assess ease, risk, owner and timing.
4. Prioritise actions into immediate, short-term and structural.
5. Avoid promising cash release.
terms.example: 1. List potential actions. 2. Quantify indicative cash effect where supportable. 3. Assess ease, risk, owner and timing. 4. Prioritise actions into immediate, short-term and structural. 5. Avoid promising cash release.
terms.commonError: • Action depends on legal/customer relationship issue.
terms.formula: Priority score = impact x urgency x feasibility, using documented scoring.
terms.howToUse:
• Actions have owners.
• Risks and dependencies noted.
terms.components: AR/AP/inventory analyses, cash forecast, issue log, client constraints.

terms.title: Reporting pack architecture
terms.definition:
Use to design management reporting pack structure. Pack architecture blueprint. 1. Define pack purpose and audience.
2. Set hierarchy: executive summary, performance, cash, forward view, risks/actions, appendices.
3. Remove duplicate or low-use pages.
4. Map every page to a decision or accountability need.
5. Agree cadence and owner.
terms.example: 1. Define pack purpose and audience. 2. Set hierarchy: executive summary, performance, cash, forward view, risks/actions, appendices. 3. Remove duplicate or low-use pages. 4. Map every page to a decision or accountability need. 5. Agree cadence and owner.
terms.commonError: • Pack tries to serve internal management and external investor purposes without separation.
terms.formula: No formula. Architecture rule: every page must have a user, decision, data source and owner.
terms.howToUse:
• No conflicting versions.
• Pack length is proportionate.
terms.components: Stakeholder map, decisions, current pack, KPIs, reporting calendar, source data.

terms.title: KPI framework design
terms.definition:
Use to select performance indicators. KPI framework. 1. Start with management objectives.
2. Select measures for financial performance, cash, operations, customer, people and risk where relevant.
3. Separate lead and lag measures.
4. Limit KPIs to those that are actionable and reliable.
5. Assign owner and cadence.
terms.example: 1. Start with management objectives. 2. Select measures for financial performance, cash, operations, customer, people and risk where relevant. 3. Separate lead and lag measures. 4. Limit KPIs to those that are actionable and reliable. 5. Assign owner and cadence.
terms.commonError:
• Vanity metrics.
• Too many KPIs.
terms.formula: No formula beyond selected KPI definitions.
terms.howToUse:
• KPI has owner/source.
• Metric can be repeated.
• Metric supports decision.
terms.components: Business objectives, operating model, current metrics, source data, stakeholder decisions.

terms.title: KPI dictionary
terms.definition:
Use to formalise KPI definitions. KPI dictionary. 1. Create one record per KPI.
2. Define formula, source, period, owner, threshold and interpretation.
3. Document exclusions and data limitations.
4. Test calculation with sample data.
5. Obtain owner sign-off.
terms.example: 1. Create one record per KPI. 2. Define formula, source, period, owner, threshold and interpretation. 3. Document exclusions and data limitations. 4. Test calculation with sample data. 5. Obtain owner sign-off.
terms.commonError: • Same KPI calculated differently by teams.
terms.formula: KPI formula must specify numerator, denominator, period and exclusions.
terms.howToUse:
• No undefined KPI.
• Source owner recorded.
terms.components: KPI list, source data, formulas, owners, thresholds.

terms.title: Lead and lag indicator mapping
terms.definition:
Use to improve forward-looking reporting. Lead/lag map. 1. Classify existing KPIs as lead, lag, diagnostic or control.
2. Check whether lag outcomes have linked lead drivers.
3. Add lead indicators only where data is reliable.
4. Map indicators to management action.
5. Review balance across financial and non-financial measures.
terms.example: 1. Classify existing KPIs as lead, lag, diagnostic or control. 2. Check whether lag outcomes have linked lead drivers. 3. Add lead indicators only where data is reliable. 4. Map indicators to management action. 5. Review balance across financial and non-financial measures.
terms.commonError: • All KPIs are backward-looking.
terms.formula: No formula. Mapping rule: lag explains result; lead signals future result.
terms.howToUse: • Each key result has at least one driver where possible.
terms.components: KPI framework, operational drivers, strategic objectives.

terms.title: Performance driver tree
terms.definition:
Use to link outcomes to operational drivers. Driver tree. 1. Start with the outcome.
2. Break into primary financial drivers.
3. Break financial drivers into operational drivers.
4. Link each driver to KPI/source.
5. Validate with process owners.
terms.example: 1. Start with the outcome. 2. Break into primary financial drivers. 3. Break financial drivers into operational drivers. 4. Link each driver to KPI/source. 5. Validate with process owners.
terms.commonError: • Driver tree built without operational input.
terms.formula: Example: Revenue = customers x orders per customer x average order value x fulfilment rate.
terms.howToUse:
• Tree reflects business logic.
• Drivers measurable.
terms.components: Objectives, KPIs, financial results, operational metrics.

terms.title: KPI thresholds and escalation
terms.definition:
Use to define when management action is required. Threshold matrix. 1. Set normal/watch/action/escalation bands.
2. Use evidence or management judgement and document basis.
3. Avoid arbitrary colour coding.
4. Assign response owner and action route.
5. Review after reporting cycles.
terms.example: 1. Set normal/watch/action/escalation bands. 2. Use evidence or management judgement and document basis. 3. Avoid arbitrary colour coding. 4. Assign response owner and action route. 5. Review after reporting cycles.
terms.commonError: • Red/amber/green without definition.
terms.formula: Thresholds may be fixed value, percentage variance, trend direction or breach condition.
terms.howToUse:
• Thresholds realistic.
• Escalation owner clear.
terms.components: Historical performance, budget, targets, risk appetite, operational constraints.

terms.title: Dashboard layout design
terms.definition:
Use for visual reporting prototypes. Dashboard wireframe. 1. Define user and decision.
2. Place critical KPIs first.
3. Use charts only where they improve understanding.
4. Show trend, status, driver and action.
5. Avoid visual clutter and unsupported automation.
terms.example: 1. Define user and decision. 2. Place critical KPIs first. 3. Use charts only where they improve understanding. 4. Show trend, status, driver and action. 5. Avoid visual clutter and unsupported automation.
terms.commonError: • Design before defining KPIs.
terms.formula: No formula. Layout rule: one page should answer what changed, why, impact, action.
terms.howToUse:
• Numbers match sources.
• Definitions visible or linked.
terms.components: KPI dictionary, user requirements, source data, reporting cadence.

terms.title: Data source mapping
terms.definition:
Use to prove repeatability of reporting. Data source map. 1. Map each output field to source system/table/report.
2. Record data owner and refresh timing.
3. Document manual transformations.
4. Identify gaps and duplicate sources.
5. Route system/integration changes to Finance Transformation.
terms.example: 1. Map each output field to source system/table/report. 2. Record data owner and refresh timing. 3. Document manual transformations. 4. Identify gaps and duplicate sources. 5. Route system/integration changes to Finance Transformation.
terms.commonError: • No owner for critical data.
terms.formula: Source map: output field -> source -> extraction -> transformation -> owner -> frequency.
terms.howToUse:
• Each key metric traceable.
• Manual steps visible.
terms.components: Systems list, reports, data owners, extracts, transformation steps.

terms.title: Reporting calendar
terms.definition:
Use to make reporting repeatable. Reporting calendar. 1. List outputs and deadlines.
2. Map data dependency and review gates.
3. Set preparation, review, issue and meeting dates.
4. Resolve bottlenecks.
5. Publish calendar with RACI.
terms.example: 1. List outputs and deadlines. 2. Map data dependency and review gates. 3. Set preparation, review, issue and meeting dates. 4. Resolve bottlenecks. 5. Publish calendar with RACI.
terms.commonError: • Reporting date before source data availability.
terms.formula: No formula.
terms.howToUse:
• Deadlines realistic.
• Review before issue.
terms.components: Report list, source availability, close timetable, meeting schedule, owners.

terms.title: Reporting RACI
terms.definition:
Use to clarify responsibility. RACI matrix. 1. List reporting outputs.
2. Assign Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed.
3. Ensure one accountable owner per output.
4. Resolve conflicts.
5. Include in reporting playbook.
terms.example: 1. List reporting outputs. 2. Assign Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. 3. Ensure one accountable owner per output. 4. Resolve conflicts. 5. Include in reporting playbook.
terms.commonError: • Unclear ownership.
terms.formula: RACI categories: R performs; A owns outcome; C gives input; I receives.
terms.howToUse:
• No output lacks owner.
• No duplicate accountability.
terms.components: Report catalogue, organisation chart, process owners.

terms.title: Action tracker
terms.definition:
Use to convert reporting into management action. Action tracker. 1. Record action, owner, due date, status and evidence needed.
2. Link action to finding or KPI breach.
3. Prioritise by impact and urgency.
4. Review at each reporting meeting.
5. Close only with evidence.
terms.example: 1. Record action, owner, due date, status and evidence needed. 2. Link action to finding or KPI breach. 3. Prioritise by impact and urgency. 4. Review at each reporting meeting. 5. Close only with evidence.
terms.commonError: • Actions without owners.
terms.formula: No formula.
terms.howToUse:
• Owner assigned.
• Evidence defined.
terms.components: Findings, review meeting notes, owners, due dates.

terms.title: Report rationalisation
terms.definition:
Use to remove duplicated or low-value reports. Report rationalisation log. 1. Catalogue reports.
2. Assess use, decision value and duplication.
3. Classify retain, amend, merge, retire.
4. Check if report has control/compliance role.
5. Recommend rationalised suite.
terms.example: 1. Catalogue reports. 2. Assess use, decision value and duplication. 3. Classify retain, amend, merge, retire. 4. Check if report has control/compliance role. 5. Recommend rationalised suite.
terms.commonError: • Retiring reports used by auditors/lenders.
terms.formula: Effort saved = estimated prep time x frequency, but do not promise savings without validation.
terms.howToUse: • No control report removed without review.
terms.components: Report catalogue, users, decisions, effort estimate, data sources.

terms.title: Reporting playbook
terms.definition:
Use to document recurring reporting rules. Reporting playbook. 1. Compile definitions and procedures.
2. Include version control and owner.
3. Keep instructions operational.
4. Cross-reference templates.
5. Review with client owner.
terms.example: 1. Compile definitions and procedures. 2. Include version control and owner. 3. Keep instructions operational. 4. Cross-reference templates. 5. Review with client owner.
terms.commonError: • Playbook too vague to operate.
terms.formula: No formula.
terms.howToUse: • All recurring outputs covered.
terms.components: KPI dictionary, calendar, RACI, data map, commentary standard, templates.

terms.title: Decision framing
terms.definition:
Use before decision-support modelling. Decision brief. 1. Write the decision question.
2. Define options and do-nothing baseline.
3. Agree criteria and constraints.
4. Confirm output use and audience.
5. Escalate regulated or out-of-scope decisions.
terms.example: 1. Write the decision question. 2. Define options and do-nothing baseline. 3. Agree criteria and constraints. 4. Confirm output use and audience. 5. Escalate regulated or out-of-scope decisions.
terms.commonError: • No clear decision owner.
terms.formula: No formula. Decision format: Should management choose option A, B or C for [objective] by [date], considering [criteria]?
terms.howToUse:
• Decision owner confirmed.
• Criteria documented.
terms.components: Decision request, decision owner, options, criteria, timeline, constraints.

terms.title: Decision data collection
terms.definition:
Use for all decision-support analyses. Decision data pack. 1. Collect only decision-relevant information.
2. Reconcile financial inputs.
3. Separate sunk, unavoidable and avoidable costs.
4. Document assumptions and excluded items.
5. Check qualitative factors.
terms.example: 1. Collect only decision-relevant information. 2. Reconcile financial inputs. 3. Separate sunk, unavoidable and avoidable costs. 4. Document assumptions and excluded items. 5. Check qualitative factors.
terms.commonError: • Including irrelevant allocated overheads.
terms.formula: Relevant cost = future cash flow that differs between options.
terms.howToUse:
• Sunk costs excluded.
• Unavoidable costs not treated as savings.
terms.components: Relevant revenues, costs, cash flows, capacity, qualitative factors, assumptions.

terms.title: Unit economics
terms.definition:
Use for per-unit profitability or cash analysis. Unit economics schedule. 1. Define unit.
2. Reconcile totals.
3. Assign direct and variable costs.
4. Calculate unit contribution and margin.
5. State limitations.
terms.example: 1. Define unit. 2. Reconcile totals. 3. Assign direct and variable costs. 4. Calculate unit contribution and margin. 5. State limitations.
terms.commonError: • Unit costs based on weak allocations.
terms.formula: Unit contribution = revenue per unit - variable/direct cost per unit. Unit margin % = unit contribution / revenue per unit.
terms.howToUse:
• Unit definition stable.
• Costs supportable.
terms.components: Unit definition, revenue, variable costs, service costs, acquisition/fulfilment data.

terms.title: Customer profitability
terms.definition:
Use to understand customer-level value. Customer profitability report. 1. Reconcile customer revenue.
2. Allocate/trace supportable costs.
3. Calculate contribution/margin.
4. Identify concentration and low-return customers.
5. Prepare cautious commentary.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile customer revenue. 2. Allocate/trace supportable costs. 3. Calculate contribution/margin. 4. Identify concentration and low-return customers. 5. Prepare cautious commentary.
terms.commonError: • Confidential customer strategy issues.
terms.formula: Customer contribution = customer revenue - customer-specific direct/variable costs.
terms.howToUse:
• Rebates included.
• Service costs considered.
terms.components: Customer revenue, discounts, rebates, direct costs, service costs, credit notes, AR data.

terms.title: Product or service profitability
terms.definition:
Use to assess product/service performance. Product/service profitability analysis. 1. Reconcile totals.
2. Check coding completeness.
3. Calculate gross/contribution/net margin as appropriate.
4. Analyse price-volume-mix and cost drivers.
5. Document allocation limitations.
terms.example: 1. Reconcile totals. 2. Check coding completeness. 3. Calculate gross/contribution/net margin as appropriate. 4. Analyse price-volume-mix and cost drivers. 5. Document allocation limitations.
terms.commonError: • Misleading allocations.
terms.formula: Product margin = product revenue - product cost base selected.
terms.howToUse:
• Definitions consistent.
• Cross-subsidies identified.
terms.components: Product/service revenue, cost of sales, direct costs, activity data, allocation bases.

terms.title: Channel or site profitability
terms.definition:
Use for channel, branch, site or location performance. Channel/site profitability report. 1. Define hierarchy.
2. Reconcile totals.
3. Separate direct and allocated costs.
4. Calculate margin and operational KPIs.
5. Explain performance with caveats.
terms.example: 1. Define hierarchy. 2. Reconcile totals. 3. Separate direct and allocated costs. 4. Calculate margin and operational KPIs. 5. Explain performance with caveats.
terms.commonError: • Using allocated overhead as direct cause.
terms.formula: Site contribution = site revenue - site direct/variable costs.
terms.howToUse:
• Unallocated costs visible.
• Operational data considered.
terms.components: Channel/site revenue, direct costs, central allocations, operational KPIs.

terms.title: Pricing support analysis
terms.definition:
Use for internal pricing decisions. Pricing support note. 1. Define pricing objective.
2. Calculate relevant cost and contribution.
3. Estimate volume/mix sensitivity.
4. Consider qualitative constraints.
5. Present options and sensitivity.
terms.example: 1. Define pricing objective. 2. Calculate relevant cost and contribution. 3. Estimate volume/mix sensitivity. 4. Consider qualitative constraints. 5. Present options and sensitivity.
terms.commonError:
• Competition law/legal advice.
• Regulated pricing.
terms.formula: Break-even volume = fixed cost / contribution per unit. Target price = relevant cost per unit + target margin, subject to market context.
terms.howToUse:
• Costs relevant.
• Capacity considered.
terms.components: Price options, relevant cost, competitor/customer context, capacity, volume assumptions.

terms.title: Make-or-buy analysis
terms.definition:
Use for outsourcing/internal production choices. Make-or-buy analysis. 1. Define options.
2. Identify relevant future cash flows.
3. Exclude sunk and unavoidable costs.
4. Consider opportunity cost of capacity.
5. Present financial and qualitative comparison.
terms.example: 1. Define options. 2. Identify relevant future cash flows. 3. Exclude sunk and unavoidable costs. 4. Consider opportunity cost of capacity. 5. Present financial and qualitative comparison.
terms.commonError: • Supplier/legal issues.
terms.formula: Decision benefit = cost avoided - external cost +/- opportunity cost/transition cost.
terms.howToUse:
• Costs truly avoidable.
• Quality and risk noted.
terms.components: Internal variable/avoidable costs, external supplier quote, capacity, quality, risk.

terms.title: Discontinue/continue analysis
terms.definition:
Use for product, service, customer or site continuation decisions. Continue/discontinue analysis. 1. Define scope.
2. Calculate lost revenue and avoidable cost.
3. Identify stranded fixed costs and transition costs.
4. Assess capacity/customer effects.
5. Escalate legal/HR/contract issues.
terms.example: 1. Define scope. 2. Calculate lost revenue and avoidable cost. 3. Identify stranded fixed costs and transition costs. 4. Assess capacity/customer effects. 5. Escalate legal/HR/contract issues.
terms.commonError: • Legal termination matters.
terms.formula: Incremental impact = revenue lost - avoidable costs saved - transition costs +/- alternative use benefit.
terms.howToUse:
• Unavoidable costs excluded from savings.
• Transition considered.
terms.components: Revenue, avoidable costs, stranded costs, capacity, contract/HR/customer implications.

terms.title: Capacity and limiting factor analysis
terms.definition:
Use where a resource constraint affects choices. Capacity analysis. 1. Identify limiting factor.
2. Calculate contribution per unit of limiting factor.
3. Rank options where appropriate.
4. Check qualitative and feasibility constraints.
5. Run sensitivity to capacity changes.
terms.example: 1. Identify limiting factor. 2. Calculate contribution per unit of limiting factor. 3. Rank options where appropriate. 4. Check qualitative and feasibility constraints. 5. Run sensitivity to capacity changes.
terms.commonError: • Multiple constraints requiring advanced optimisation.
terms.formula: Contribution per limiting factor = contribution per unit / limiting factor units per unit.
terms.howToUse:
• Constraint correctly identified.
• Demand/capacity assumptions checked.
terms.components: Products/options, contribution, resource usage, available capacity.

terms.title: Business case model
terms.definition:
Use for internal project, hiring, expansion or investment support. Business case model and note. 1. Define objective and baseline.
2. Build transparent inputs/calculations/outputs.
3. Model profit, cash and timing.
4. Include sensitivity and qualitative factors.
5. Avoid investment advice or valuation opinion wording.
terms.example: 1. Define objective and baseline. 2. Build transparent inputs/calculations/outputs. 3. Model profit, cash and timing. 4. Include sensitivity and qualitative factors. 5. Avoid investment advice or valuation opinion wording.
terms.commonError: • Valuation or regulated investment advice.
terms.formula: Common outputs: net cash impact, payback, ROI, NPV if in scope. Use NPV only with agreed discount rate and purpose.
terms.howToUse:
• Assumptions owned.
• No hidden hardcodes.
• Sensitivity included.
terms.components: Baseline, options, costs, benefits, cash flows, assumptions, risks.

terms.title: Options comparison matrix
terms.definition:
Use to present decision alternatives. Options comparison. 1. List options including do-nothing.
2. Use consistent criteria.
3. Score or rank only where criteria are agreed.
4. Show trade-offs and limitations.
5. Present management decision points.
terms.example: 1. List options including do-nothing. 2. Use consistent criteria. 3. Score or rank only where criteria are agreed. 4. Show trade-offs and limitations. 5. Present management decision points.
terms.commonError: • Model decides for management.
terms.formula: Weighted score = sum(score x weight), only where weights are agreed.
terms.howToUse:
• Weights/criteria documented.
• No false precision.
terms.components: Decision criteria, option analyses, qualitative factors, risks, sensitivities.

terms.title: Cross-check review
terms.definition:
Use before any client issue. Cross-check checklist. 1. Tie every number to source.
2. Cross-cast tables and charts.
3. Check commentary against data.
4. Confirm unresolved issues and limitations.
5. Obtain review clearance.

terms.title: Use and control of these method notes

terms.title: Standard technical workflow
terms.definition: Confirm reporting framework, reporting period, reporting entity, comparatives, group structure, functional/presentation currency and local endorsement position. Reconcile trial balances, general ledger exports, subledgers and prior-year accounts before performing IFRS analysis.
terms.example: Record every proposed adjustment in the IFRS adjustment register. Prepare technical memos for judgemental matters.
terms.commonError: Do not mark a standard as not applicable solely because the trial balance does not show an obvious account name. Do not draft disclosures from memory.
terms.howToUse: Obtain partner review for all material, judgemental, externally sensitive or unsupported matters before client issue.

terms.title: IFRS 1 - First-time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards
terms.definition: first IFRS financial statements; local GAAP to IFRS conversion; investor/lender/group requirement for IFRS information Transition memo; IFRS 1 exemption/exception schedule; opening IFRS position; adjustment register; equity/profit reconciliations
terms.example: Confirm transition date, first IFRS reporting period and comparative period. Build the opening IFRS statement of financial position from the previous GAAP trial balance. Review mandatory exceptions before optional exemptions. Prepare reconciliation from previous GAAP equity/profit to IFRS equity/profit. Record every conversion adjustment with debit/credit, tax effect and disclosure effect.
terms.commonError: Unsupported opening balances; hindsight-sensitive estimates; optional exemption judgement; material adjustments.

terms.title: IFRS 2 - Share-based Payment
terms.definition: share options, warrants, founder/employee/adviser equity awards, cash-settled awards or modifications Scheme inventory; classification memo; expense model; reserve/liability reconciliation; disclosure schedule
terms.example: List every award. Classify as equity-settled, cash-settled or settlement-choice. Identify grant date, vesting conditions, service period and market/non-market conditions. Check valuation inputs. Recalculate cumulative expense, reserve or liability movement by tranche. Review modifications/cancellations separately.
terms.commonError: Unsupported valuation inputs; modified awards; unclear settlement terms; complex performance conditions.

terms.title: IFRS 3 - Business Combinations
terms.definition: acquisition of a business, subsidiary, trade, customer base, business combination, goodwill or bargain purchase Business-versus-asset assessment; acquisition accounting workbook; consideration schedule; fair value schedules; goodwill calculation
terms.example: First decide business combination versus asset acquisition. Identify acquirer and acquisition date from control transfer evidence. Build consideration schedule, including contingent consideration. Identify separately recognisable assets/liabilities. Calculate goodwill or bargain purchase. Track measurement-period adjustments.
terms.commonError: All business-combination conclusions; bargain purchase; contingent consideration; intangible recognition; fair value uncertainty.

terms.title: IFRS 5 - Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations
terms.definition: planned disposal of asset, subsidiary, business line or disposal group; board-approved sale; discontinued operation presentation Held-for-sale checklist; measurement schedule; discontinued operation memo; disclosure support
terms.example: Check held-for-sale criteria: available for immediate sale, committed plan and highly probable sale. Measure at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Stop depreciation/amortisation from classification date where required. Assess discontinued operation classification separately.
terms.commonError: Weak sale probability; unsupported fair value; disposal group liabilities; covenant/stakeholder impact.

terms.title: IFRS 6 - Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources
terms.definition: exploration and evaluation activity in extractive industries Specialist screen; E&E asset schedule; impairment trigger note; partner handoff
terms.example: Screen only. Identify exploration/evaluation assets and related policy. Check impairment trigger requirements and IAS 36 handoff. Do not perform specialist extractive-sector work without partner approval.
terms.commonError: Any extractive activity with material balances or policy judgement.

terms.title: IFRS 7 - Financial Instruments: Disclosures
terms.definition: financial instruments, loans, receivables, payables, derivatives, guarantees, investments, material financial risks Financial instruments disclosure workbook; risk disclosure schedules; liquidity maturity table; fair value hierarchy support
terms.example: Prepare financial instrument inventory by class and measurement category. Reconcile to trial balance. Prepare credit, liquidity and market risk disclosure support. Prepare fair value hierarchy and sensitivity information where required. Tie to IFRS 9, IFRS 13 and IAS 32.
terms.commonError: Derivatives; Level 3 fair values; covenants; material credit concentrations; complex risk disclosure judgement.

terms.title: IFRS 8 - Operating Segments
terms.definition: listed/publicly accountable entity, internal segment reports reviewed by CODM, investor pack divisional reporting CODM memo; segment assessment; reportable segment calculation; reconciliation schedule; disclosure support

terms.commonError: Aggregation decisions; changes in CODM reporting; major customer concentration; mismatch with investor reporting.

terms.title: IFRS 9 - Financial Instruments
