terms.commonError: Derivatives; hedging; convertible instruments; debt restructuring; covenant default; material ECL assumptions.

terms.title: IFRS 10 - Consolidated Financial Statements
terms.definition: subsidiaries, de facto control, structured entities, complex ownership rights Control assessment file; consolidation population; exclusion rationale; handoff memo
terms.example: Identify all investees. Assess power over relevant activities, exposure to variable returns and ability to use power to affect returns. Do not rely only on ownership percentage. Document consolidation population and exclusions. Hand off to consolidation team.
terms.commonError: Structured entities; protective versus substantive rights; investment entity assessment; loss of control.

terms.title: IFRS 11 - Joint Arrangements
terms.definition: joint venture, joint operation, consortium, partnership or unanimous consent arrangements Joint control assessment; classification memo; accounting handoff; IFRS 12 input
terms.example: Confirm joint control. Classify arrangement as joint operation or joint venture using legal form, contractual rights and other facts. For joint operations, identify rights to assets and obligations for liabilities. For joint ventures, prepare IAS 28 equity accounting handoff.
terms.commonError: Vehicle-based arrangements; unclear rights/obligations; contractual terms overriding legal form.

terms.title: IFRS 12 - Disclosure of Interests in Other Entities
terms.definition: subsidiaries, associates, joint arrangements, structured entities or material NCI Interests register; judgement disclosure support; NCI schedules; summarised financial information
terms.example: Create interests register. Document significant control/influence judgements. Prepare NCI, restrictions and summarised financial information schedules. Assess unconsolidated structured entity exposure. Reconcile to IFRS 10, IFRS 11 and IAS 28 conclusions.
terms.commonError: Significant judgements; restrictions on cash/assets; structured entity exposure; material NCI.

terms.title: IFRS 13 - Fair Value Measurement
terms.definition: assets/liabilities measured or disclosed at fair value under other standards Fair value register; valuation evidence; hierarchy classification; sensitivity support
terms.example: Identify all fair value measurements/disclosures. Confirm unit of account, market assumptions and valuation technique. Classify Level 1/2/3 by observability of inputs. Reconcile valuation outputs to ledger. Prepare sensitivity disclosures for material Level 3 items.
terms.commonError: Unsupported valuation; Level 3 measurements; specialist valuation requirement; management bias risk.

terms.title: IFRS 14 - Regulatory Deferral Accounts
terms.definition: rate-regulated activities by first-time adopter eligible to apply standard IFRS 14 eligibility screen; rate-regulated balances note
terms.example: Screen only. Confirm first-time adopter status and rate-regulated activity. Do not apply to existing IFRS reporter. Obtain partner approval before any recognition or presentation work.
terms.commonError: Any possible regulatory deferral balance or sector-specific judgement.

terms.title: IFRS 15 - Revenue from Contracts with Customers
terms.definition: customer contracts, subscriptions, milestones, licences, rebates, warranties, refunds or variable consideration Revenue contract inventory; five-step model matrix; timing assessment; contract balance reconciliation; disclosure gap list
terms.example: Map material revenue streams through contract identification, performance obligations, transaction price, allocation and timing. Assess point-in-time versus over-time recognition. Review variable consideration constraints, principal-agent issues, contract assets/liabilities and disclosure requirements.
terms.commonError: Bundled contracts; long-term contracts; variable consideration; principal-agent; licences; side letters.

terms.title: IFRS 16 - Leases
terms.definition: property, vehicles, equipment, embedded leases, service contracts with identified assets Lease population schedule; lease term memo; IFRS 16 workbook; modification log; disclosure tie-out
terms.example: Build complete lease population. Identify leases and terms, including renewal/termination options. Recalculate ROU assets and lease liabilities using supported payment schedules and discount rates. Review modifications, exemptions and disclosures.
terms.commonError: Embedded leases; unsupported discount rates; significant renewal options; incomplete population.

terms.title: IFRS 17 - Insurance Contracts
terms.definition: insurance contracts, reinsurance, insurer activities or contracts transferring significant insurance risk IFRS 17 applicability screen; contract inventory; specialist handoff note
terms.example: Specialist screen. Determine whether contracts may fall within IFRS 17. Do not scope technical measurement without expertise and partner approval. Coordinate evidence and specialist handoff only unless explicitly contracted.
terms.commonError: Any possible insurance contract or reinsurance arrangement.

terms.title: IFRS 18 - Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements
terms.definition: 2027 readiness, early adoption, statement presentation, MPMs, subtotals and disaggregation IFRS 18 readiness checklist; presentation mapping; MPM inventory; disclosure impact note
terms.example: For applicable periods or readiness work, map current statement presentation to IFRS 18 categories, required subtotals, aggregation/disaggregation and management-defined performance measures. Do not early-adopt without client governance and partner approval.
terms.commonError: Early adoption; investor communications; MPM definitions; comparatives and systems impact.

terms.title: IFRS 19 - Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures
terms.definition: eligible subsidiary considering reduced disclosures from 2027 Eligibility screen; election note; disclosure impact schedule
terms.example: Screen eligibility: subsidiary, no public accountability, parent produces IFRS consolidated financial statements available for public use. If eligible and elected, retain recognition/measurement from other IFRS Standards and use reduced disclosure requirements.
terms.commonError: Eligibility uncertainty; public accountability; client wants automatic reduced disclosures; group reporting implications.

terms.title: IAS 1 - Presentation of Financial Statements
terms.definition: current presentation framework before IFRS 18 adoption; complete financial statements; IFRS compliance statement IAS 1 presentation checklist; compliance statement support; going concern issue note
terms.example: For pre-IFRS 18 periods, check complete set of financial statements, comparatives, going concern, current/non-current classification, offsetting, fair presentation and explicit IFRS compliance statement. Hand off future periods to IFRS 18 readiness.
terms.commonError: Material departure from IFRS; going concern uncertainty; early IFRS 18 transition.

terms.title: IAS 2 - Inventories
terms.definition: stock, WIP, finished goods, obsolescence, NRV risk Inventory reconciliation; costing memo; NRV assessment; write-down schedule
terms.example: Reconcile inventory to subledger/physical reports. Check cost formula, overhead allocation and excluded costs. Compare carrying amount to NRV. Review obsolescence and write-down/reversal evidence.
terms.commonError: Unreconciled inventory; weak costing; obsolete stock; material overhead judgement.

terms.title: IAS 7 - Statement of Cash Flows
terms.definition: cash flow statement preparation and financing liability reconciliation Cash flow workbook; cash equivalent assessment; financing liability reconciliation
terms.example: Prepare cash flow from audited/reconciled balance sheet movements and P&L. Classify operating, investing and financing cash flows. Reconcile cash/cash equivalents and financing liability movements, including non-cash changes.
terms.commonError: Classification judgement; restricted cash; non-cash transactions; financing movements do not reconcile.

terms.title: IAS 8 - Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors
terms.definition: policy selection, policy changes, estimates, prior-period errors or restatements IAS 8 issue memo; restatement schedule; estimate change log
terms.example: Identify whether issue is policy, estimate or error. Determine whether retrospective restatement or prospective treatment is required. Record facts, basis and financial/disclosure impact. Do not restate prior periods without partner review.
terms.commonError: Prior-period error; change in policy; management wants presentation without restatement support.

terms.title: IAS 10 - Events after the Reporting Period
terms.definition: events between reporting date and authorisation date Subsequent events schedule; adjusting/non-adjusting assessment; disclosure note
terms.example: Obtain board minutes, management updates, financing events, litigation updates and covenant information. Classify events as adjusting or non-adjusting. Assess going concern impact and disclosure.
terms.commonError: Going concern impact; material transaction; litigation; financing/covenant event.

terms.title: IAS 12 - Income Taxes
terms.definition: current tax, deferred tax, temporary differences, losses or uncertain tax treatments Tax accounting schedule; deferred tax matrix; losses assessment; tax disclosure support
terms.example: Reconcile tax balances to computations where available. Identify temporary differences and deferred tax assets/liabilities. Assess recoverability of tax losses using supportable forecasts. Consider uncertain tax treatment disclosure/measurement support.
terms.commonError: Tax filing advice request; uncertain positions; losses; complex group tax; conversion tax effects.

terms.title: IAS 16 - Property, Plant and Equipment
terms.definition: PPE additions, disposals, depreciation, revaluation, componentisation PPE reconciliation; depreciation recalculation; capitalisation memo; disposal schedule
terms.example: Reconcile fixed asset register to TB. Check recognition, useful lives, depreciation method, componentisation, capital versus repair decisions and disposals. Review revaluation evidence if revaluation model applies.
terms.commonError: Large capex; weak useful life evidence; revaluation; impairment indicator.

terms.title: IAS 19 - Employee Benefits
terms.definition: pensions, bonuses, holiday pay, termination benefits, long-term employee benefits Benefits inventory; payroll accrual schedule; actuarial report tie-out; disclosure support
terms.example: Identify benefit types. Reconcile accruals and payroll-related balances. For defined benefit plans, obtain actuarial report and check inputs to financial statements. Review termination benefit triggers and disclosures.
terms.commonError: Defined benefit schemes; actuarial assumptions; restructuring/termination benefits.

terms.title: IAS 20 - Government Grants
terms.definition: grants, subsidies, forgivable loans or assistance Grant register; condition assessment; recognition schedule; disclosure support
terms.example: Obtain grant agreements and conditions. Determine whether conditions are met and whether grant relates to income or assets. Review recognition pattern, presentation and disclosure.
terms.commonError: Unmet conditions; repayment risk; grant linked to assets or performance milestones.

terms.title: IAS 21 - Foreign Exchange
terms.definition: foreign currency transactions, foreign operations, translation reserves, functional currency judgement Functional currency memo; FX translation workbook; reserve reconciliation
terms.example: Confirm functional currency using primary economic environment evidence. Recalculate monetary items using closing rates and transactions using appropriate rates. Translate foreign operations and reconcile exchange reserves.
terms.commonError: Functional currency change; long-term intercompany funding; hyperinflation interaction; material FX movements.

terms.title: IAS 23 - Borrowing Costs
terms.definition: qualifying assets and capitalised interest Borrowing cost calculation; qualifying asset memo; interest reconciliation
terms.example: Identify qualifying assets. Determine capitalisation period and eligible borrowings. Recalculate capitalised borrowing costs. Stop capitalisation when asset is ready for intended use.
terms.commonError: Large development projects; mixed funding; suspended construction; material judgement.

terms.title: IAS 24 - Related Party Disclosures
terms.definition: group companies, directors, key management personnel, shareholders and related transactions Related party register; transactions schedule; disclosure support
terms.example: Identify related parties from registers, board minutes, group chart and management enquiry. Reconcile balances, transactions and commitments. Prepare KMP compensation support.
terms.commonError: Incomplete management declaration; unusual transactions; undisclosed guarantees/commitments.

terms.title: IAS 26 - Accounting and Reporting by Retirement Benefit Plans
terms.definition: reporting entity is a retirement benefit plan IAS 26 eligibility screen; plan reporting evidence; specialist handoff
terms.example: Specialist screen. Confirm the entity is a retirement benefit plan, not merely an employer. Obtain actuarial and plan asset information. Do not perform actuarial measurement.
terms.commonError: Any material plan reporting issue or lack of actuarial support.

terms.title: IAS 27 - Separate Financial Statements
terms.definition: parent/investor separate financial statements Separate FS investment schedule; policy memo; impairment screen
terms.example: Identify investments in subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures in separate accounts. Confirm selected accounting policy and apply consistently. Reconcile dividend income and impairment indicators.
terms.commonError: Policy inconsistency; impairment; legal entity reporting sensitivity.

terms.title: IAS 28 - Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures
terms.definition: significant influence or joint venture equity accounting IAS 28 assessment; equity accounting workbook; impairment screen
terms.example: Assess significant influence. Obtain associate/JV financials. Calculate equity-accounted share of profit/loss, OCI, dividends, impairment and carrying amount. Align accounting policies where material.
terms.commonError: Losses exceed investment; non-coterminous year ends; policy differences; impairment.

terms.title: IAS 29 - Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies
terms.definition: entities whose functional currency is hyperinflationary Hyperinflation screen; restatement workbook; translation note
terms.example: Screen jurisdiction and functional currency. If applicable, restate non-monetary items and statement of comprehensive income using a general price index. Assess IAS 21 translation interaction.
terms.commonError: Any hyperinflation application or presentation currency interaction.

terms.title: IAS 32 - Financial Instruments: Presentation
terms.definition: equity/liability classification, offsetting, compound instruments IAS 32 classification memo; offsetting assessment; compound instrument schedule
terms.example: Review contractual substance for debt/equity classification. Split compound instruments if required. Assess offsetting criteria. Coordinate with IFRS 7 and IFRS 9.
terms.commonError: Convertible debt; preference shares; puttable instruments; offsetting arrangements.

terms.title: IAS 33 - Earnings per Share
terms.definition: listed/publicly traded entity or entity presenting EPS EPS workbook; share reconciliation; dilution assessment
terms.example: Confirm applicability. Calculate basic EPS using profit attributable to ordinary shareholders and weighted average shares. Calculate diluted EPS for options, convertibles or contingently issuable shares. Reconcile numerator/denominator.
terms.commonError: Complex capital structure; loss-making entity; convertible instruments; share restructuring.

terms.title: IAS 34 - Interim Financial Reporting
terms.definition: interim financial statements or investor/lender interim IFRS pack Interim reporting checklist; significant events schedule; condensed statements
terms.example: Confirm whether IAS 34 applies. Prepare condensed primary statements and selected explanatory notes. Focus on significant events, transactions, estimates and changes since annual reporting date.
terms.commonError: Public interim reporting; unusual transactions; major estimates; going concern/covenant events.

terms.title: IAS 36 - Impairment of Assets
terms.definition: impairment indicators, goodwill, intangibles, PPE, ROU assets, investments Impairment indicator checklist; CGU memo; model review; sensitivity schedule
terms.example: Screen indicators. Identify CGUs. Review recoverable amount model: value in use or fair value less costs of disposal. Check cash flows, growth, discount rate and sensitivity. Record impairment or reversal rules.
terms.commonError: Goodwill/indefinite intangibles; unsupported forecasts; discount rates; covenant or investor implications.

terms.title: IAS 37 - Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
terms.definition: legal claims, onerous contracts, restructuring, warranties, disputes, decommissioning Provisions register; recognition assessment; measurement schedule; disclosure support
terms.example: List obligations and contingencies from legal letters, board minutes, contracts and management enquiry. Assess present obligation, probability and reliable estimate. Measure best estimate and discount if material. Prepare contingent disclosure where not recognised.
terms.commonError: Legal uncertainty; restructuring; onerous contracts; material contingent liability.

terms.title: IAS 38 - Intangible Assets
terms.definition: software, development costs, acquired intangibles, licences, brands or customer relationships Intangible asset register; R&D analysis; amortisation schedule; impairment screen
terms.example: Reconcile intangible assets. Separate research from development. Capitalise development only when criteria are evidenced. Check amortisation, useful life and impairment. Coordinate acquired intangibles with IFRS 3.
terms.commonError: Internally generated assets; software capitalisation; indefinite lives; acquired intangibles.

terms.title: IAS 39 - Financial Instruments: Recognition and Measurement
terms.definition: limited residual hedge accounting or legacy circumstances where IAS 39 is still relevant IAS 39 residual screen; hedge documentation; partner approval note
terms.example: Confirm IFRS 9 applies. Use IAS 39 only where permitted continuation of hedge accounting or legacy issue is valid. Obtain formal policy election and hedge documentation. Partner approval required before any IAS 39 treatment.
terms.commonError: Any proposed IAS 39 treatment in current-period financial statements.

terms.title: IAS 40 - Investment Property
terms.definition: property held for rental income or capital appreciation Investment property classification memo; measurement schedule; valuation support
terms.example: Classify property as owner-occupied, inventory or investment property based on use. Confirm measurement model: fair value or cost. Tie fair value to valuation evidence and prepare disclosures.
terms.commonError: Mixed-use property; fair value uncertainty; transfers in/out; restrictions.

terms.title: IAS 41 - Agriculture
terms.definition: biological assets and agricultural produce Biological asset register; valuation schedule; quantity reconciliation; disclosure support
terms.example: Identify biological assets and agricultural produce. Measure biological assets and harvested produce using appropriate fair value less costs to sell model where required. Reconcile physical quantities to valuation and ledger.
terms.commonError: Valuation inputs; immature assets; lack of market data; material quantity discrepancies.

terms.title: Final technical completion gate
terms.definition: Every applicable standard has a working paper or reasoned non-applicability note. Every proposed adjustment has an evidence reference, debit/credit, tax effect and disclosure impact. Every significant judgement or estimate has a memo and partner review status.
terms.example: IFRS 18, IFRS 19 and other future-effective requirements are labelled as readiness or transition matters unless adopted in the current reporting period.
terms.commonError: It does not expand the Statement of Work.

terms.title: Reference control
terms.definition: • IFRS Foundation - IFRS Accounting Standards Navigator: primary confirmation point for current Standards and related materials. • IFRS Foundation - IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements: effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted.
terms.example: • IFRS Foundation - IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures: effective for annual reporting periods on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted.
terms.commonError: It does not expand the Statement of Work.

packs.label: Merixa IFRS Reporting Technical Accounting Standards Guideline

terms.title: IFRS 1 - First-time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Transition to IFRS, opening IFRS statement of financial position, mandatory exceptions, optional exemptions, comparative period restatement and transition adjustment register. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has not previously issued IFRS financial statements; Client is converting from UK GAAP, local GAAP or management accounts to IFRS; Investor, lender or group requirement requests IFRS-compliant information Minimum evidence to obtain: Previous GAAP financial statements and trial balances; Transition date agreed with partner; Accounting policy comparison; Opening balance sheet source schedules; List of selected IFRS 1 exemptions and mandatory exceptions Mandatory work steps: IFRS 1.1 Confirm the first IFRS reporting period, the transition date and the comparative period.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not post adjustments before the policy basis is reviewed.
terms.howToUse: Record them in the engagement control sheet. Document why each selected exemption is suitable.

terms.title: IFRS 2 - Share-based Payment
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Classification and measurement of equity-settled, cash-settled and choice-of-settlement awards, including vesting conditions, fair value inputs, modifications and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Share options, warrants, management incentive plans or employee equity awards exist; Founder, employee, adviser or supplier receives equity or equity-linked compensation; Awards have been modified, cancelled or settled Minimum evidence to obtain: Award agreements and scheme rules; Grant dates and vesting schedules; Employee/service recipient listing; Fair value valuation report or inputs; Modification and cancellation documentation Mandatory work steps: IFRS 2.1 List every share-based arrangement.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not assume equity settlement from the legal label alone.
terms.howToUse: Record valuation inputs used. Reconcile to payroll, equity and liability accounts. Document incremental fair value or revised measurement impact.

terms.title: IFRS 3 - Business Combinations
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Business versus asset acquisition assessment, acquisition date, consideration transferred, identifiable assets and liabilities, NCI, goodwill or bargain purchase, and measurement period accounting.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Entity acquired a business, subsidiary, trade, customer base or set of assets; Group restructuring includes acquisition accounting; Goodwill, bargain purchase or fair value uplift exists Minimum evidence to obtain: SPA and completion documents; Completion accounts; Consideration schedule including contingent consideration; Fair value reports; Opening balance sheet of acquiree; NCI and ownership schedule Mandatory work steps: IFRS 3.1 Confirm whether the acquisition is a business combination or an asset acquisition.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Document the analysis; do not assume acquisition accounting applies.
terms.howToUse: Document the analysis; do not assume acquisition accounting applies.

terms.title: IFRS 5 - Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Held-for-sale classification, disposal groups, measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, discontinued operation presentation and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Asset, subsidiary, business line or disposal group is planned for sale; Board has approved disposal; Operation has ceased or is classified as discontinued; Assets are presented separately as held for sale Minimum evidence to obtain: Board approval and disposal plan; Broker/offer/marketing evidence; Expected completion timetable; Carrying amount schedule; Fair value less costs to sell evidence Mandatory work steps: IFRS 5.1 Confirm that management is committed to the sale and the asset or disposal group is available for immediate sale in its present condition.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not use discontinued operation presentation merely because management views it as non-core.
terms.howToUse: Obtain evidence of active marketing and expected completion. Record any impairment before presentation.

terms.title: IFRS 7 - Financial Instruments: Disclosures
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Financial instrument disclosures covering significance, categories, credit risk, liquidity risk, market risk, fair value hierarchy, sensitivity and risk management information. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has loans, receivables, payables, derivatives, investments, guarantees or other financial instruments; Financial risks are material or lender/investor reporting is required Minimum evidence to obtain: Financial instruments listing; Debt agreements; Derivative confirmations; Aged receivables; Liquidity maturity profile; Fair value hierarchy assessment; Risk management policy Mandatory work steps: IFRS 7.1 Prepare a complete financial instruments inventory by class, carrying amount and IFRS 9 measurement category.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IFRS 8 - Operating Segments
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Identification of operating segments using internal CODM reporting, aggregation, reportable segment thresholds, reconciliations and entity-wide disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client is listed or otherwise required to provide segment reporting; Internal management reporting is reviewed by CODM; Investor pack uses divisional, regional or product reporting Minimum evidence to obtain: Board and executive reporting packs; CODM identification; Internal segment results; Organisational charts; Segment asset/liability data if reviewed internally Mandatory work steps: IFRS 8.1 Confirm whether IFRS 8 applies to the reporting entity.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not prepare segment notes for entities outside scope unless requested for management purposes.

terms.title: IFRS 9 - Financial Instruments
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Classification and measurement, expected credit loss impairment, hedge accounting, modifications, derecognition and financial guarantee treatment. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Financial assets, receivables, loans, investments, debt instruments, derivatives, guarantees or hedges exist; Trade receivables have impairment risk; Debt has been refinanced or modified Minimum evidence to obtain: Instrument contracts; Business model assessment; SPPI analysis; Receivables ageing; Historical loss data; Forward-looking information; Hedge documentation; Modification terms Mandatory work steps: IFRS 9.1 Compile a complete financial instruments population and reconcile to the trial balance.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.
terms.howToUse: Record the conclusion for each class. Use supportable historical and forward-looking assumptions.

terms.title: IFRS 10 - Consolidated Financial Statements
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Control assessment and handoff to consolidation team for entities requiring group reporting treatment. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has subsidiaries, special purpose entities, de facto control, protective rights or structured entities; Ownership percentage does not match control conclusion Minimum evidence to obtain: Group structure chart; Shareholder agreements; Articles/constitutional documents; Board appointment rights; Voting rights; Relevant activity decision rights Mandatory work steps: IFRS 10.1 Identify all investees and entities connected to the client group.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. IFRS 10.3 Do not rely solely on percentage ownership.
terms.howToUse: Review contractual rights, board rights and practical ability to direct activities.

terms.title: IFRS 11 - Joint Arrangements
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Classification of joint arrangements as joint operations or joint ventures and accounting handoff. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Joint venture, consortium, partnership, collaboration agreement or jointly controlled activity exists; Unanimous consent is required for relevant activities Minimum evidence to obtain: Joint arrangement agreement; Legal vehicle documents; Rights to assets and obligations for liabilities; Decision-making terms; Output purchase or funding commitments Mandatory work steps: IFRS 11.1 Confirm whether joint control exists by checking whether relevant activity decisions require unanimous consent.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IFRS 12 - Disclosure of Interests in Other Entities
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Disclosure of subsidiaries, associates, joint arrangements, unconsolidated structured entities and significant judgements about control or influence. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, joint operations, structured entities or material non-controlling interests Minimum evidence to obtain: Group structure; Control and influence assessments; NCI schedules; Summarised financial information; Restrictions on assets or cash transfer Mandatory work steps: IFRS 12.1 Create a full interests-in-other-entities register covering subsidiaries, associates, joint arrangements and structured entities.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IFRS 13 - Fair Value Measurement
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Fair value measurement framework, valuation basis, principal market, highest and best use, hierarchy, inputs, techniques and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Assets or liabilities are measured or disclosed at fair value; Valuation reports are used; Investment property, derivatives, contingent consideration or financial instruments are material Minimum evidence to obtain: Valuation reports; Market data; Input assumptions; Management valuation models; Fair value hierarchy evidence; Sensitivity analysis Mandatory work steps: IFRS 13.1 Identify every balance measured or disclosed at fair value under another IFRS standard.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not accept unexplained valuation models.

terms.title: IFRS 14 - Regulatory Deferral Accounts
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Specialist screen for first-time adopters with rate-regulated activities and regulatory deferral account balances. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client is a first-time adopter with rate-regulated activities; Previous GAAP includes regulatory deferral account balances; Utilities or regulated infrastructure activity exists Minimum evidence to obtain: Regulator framework; Previous GAAP accounting policy; Regulatory asset/liability balances; Rate-setting documentation; Transition analysis Mandatory work steps: IFRS 14.1 Confirm whether the entity is a first-time adopter and whether IFRS 14 is available.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not apply IFRS 14 to entities already reporting under IFRS.

terms.title: IFRS 15 - Revenue from Contracts with Customers
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Five-step revenue model, performance obligations, variable consideration, timing of recognition, contract balances, contract costs and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client earns revenue from contracts with customers; Contracts include milestones, bundles, variable pricing, rebates, warranties, licences, subscriptions, upfront fees or long-term delivery Minimum evidence to obtain: Customer contract population; Sample contracts by revenue stream; Order and invoice data; Delivery evidence; Rebate/discount schedules; Contract asset/liability reconciliations Mandatory work steps: IFRS 15.1 Segment revenue streams by contract type and commercial model.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not test only the general ledger.
terms.howToUse: Challenge bundled goods, services, licences, installation and support elements.

terms.title: IFRS 16 - Leases
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Lease population completeness, lease identification, right-of-use assets, lease liabilities, discount rates, modifications, exemptions and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client uses property, vehicles, equipment, embedded arrangements, service contracts with identified assets, sale-and-leaseback or lease modifications Minimum evidence to obtain: Lease agreements; Property schedule; Supplier contracts; Payment schedules; IBR support; Modification documents; Short-term/low-value exemption list Mandatory work steps: IFRS 16.1 Build a complete lease population from general ledger payments, property listings, supplier data and management enquiry.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not rely only on formal lease register.
terms.howToUse: Obtain support for incremental borrowing rate.

terms.title: IFRS 17 - Insurance Contracts
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Specialist screen for insurance and reinsurance contracts. This standard must not be scoped for delivery without appropriate expertise and partner approval. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client issues insurance contracts; Client holds reinsurance contracts; Warranty, guarantee or service arrangement may transfer significant insurance risk Minimum evidence to obtain: Insurance/reinsurance contracts; Product terms; Risk transfer assessment; Actuarial models if available; Prior actuarial/accounting papers Mandatory work steps: IFRS 17.1 Screen whether contracts transfer significant insurance risk.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not classify based on product name alone.

terms.title: IFRS 18 - Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Readiness for 2027 presentation and disclosure requirements, defined subtotals, management-defined performance measures, aggregation and disaggregation, and IAS 1 replacement. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client prepares IFRS financial statements for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027; Client is preparing comparatives for IFRS 18 adoption; Management uses alternative performance measures in public or investor communications Minimum evidence to obtain: Current financial statement format; Management accounts and investor presentations; Current subtotals/APMs/MPMs; Chart of accounts and mapping; Disclosure notes Mandatory work steps: IFRS 18.1 Confirm effective date and whether early adoption is intended.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. IFRS 18.7 Do not remove IAS 1 checks for periods before IFRS 18 becomes effective.
terms.howToUse: Record the period of first application and comparative periods affected. Challenge generic or mixed-nature line items. Use the current applicable standard for the reporting period.

terms.title: IFRS 19 - Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Eligibility, election and reduced disclosure application for qualifying subsidiaries while recognition and measurement requirements remain under other IFRS Accounting Standards. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Entity is a subsidiary without public accountability; Parent prepares publicly available IFRS consolidated financial statements; Client wants reduced disclosure financial statements Minimum evidence to obtain: Group structure; Public accountability assessment; Parent financial statements; Board election; Disclosure comparison Mandatory work steps: IFRS 19.1 Confirm the entity is a subsidiary and assess whether it has public accountability.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not assume private company status is sufficient.
terms.howToUse: Use IFRS 19 only for disclosure requirements.

terms.title: IAS 2 - Inventories
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Inventory recognition, cost formula, overhead allocation, net realisable value, obsolescence, write-downs, reversals and disclosure. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client holds stock, work in progress, raw materials, finished goods or goods for resale; Inventory valuation or obsolescence is material Minimum evidence to obtain: Inventory listing; Stock count results; Costing method; Overhead allocation; Sales after year end; Obsolescence provision; NRV analysis Mandatory work steps: IAS 2.1 Reconcile inventory listing to the general ledger and stock count evidence.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not offset unsupported categories.

terms.title: IAS 7 - Statement of Cash Flows
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Cash flow statement classification, operating/investing/financing sections, non-cash movements, cash equivalents and financing liability reconciliation. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Financial statements include cash flow statement; Client has debt, leases, acquisitions, disposals, non-cash transactions or complex cash equivalents Minimum evidence to obtain: Trial balance movements; Bank reconciliations; Debt and lease movement schedules; Capex schedules; Tax/interest paid data; Acquisition/disposal cash data Mandatory work steps: IAS 7.1 Confirm the cash and cash equivalents definition and reconcile to bank and cash ledger accounts.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. IAS 7.2 Prepare the cash flow statement from ledger movements and supporting schedules; do not rely on unexplained system outputs.

terms.title: IAS 8 - Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Accounting policy selection, changes in policy, changes in estimates, prior-period errors, retrospective restatement and disclosure. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client changes accounting policy or estimate; Prior-period error identified; No specific IFRS standard clearly applies; Restatement may be needed Minimum evidence to obtain: Prior year financial statements; Policy documents; Error analysis; Estimate assumptions; Management papers; Materiality assessment Mandatory work steps: IAS 8.1 Identify whether the matter is a policy change, estimate change or prior-period error.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 10 - Events after the Reporting Period
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Identification of adjusting and non-adjusting events after reporting date, disclosure of material non-adjusting events and going concern effects. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Material events occur between reporting date and authorisation date; Management announces restructuring, financing, acquisition, litigation outcome, impairment event or going concern issue Minimum evidence to obtain: Board minutes after year end; Management representation; Legal updates; Bank correspondence; Post-year-end sales and collections; Authorisation date Mandatory work steps: IAS 10.1 Confirm the date financial statements are authorised for issue and who authorises them.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 12 - Income Taxes
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Current tax, deferred tax, temporary differences, tax losses, uncertain tax treatments, tax rate changes and disclosures for financial reporting purposes. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has taxable profits/losses, deferred tax balances, tax losses, uncertain tax treatments, business combinations or timing differences Minimum evidence to obtain: Tax computations; Fixed asset tax basis; Loss schedules; Temporary difference analysis; Tax authority correspondence; Rate information; Business combination fair values Mandatory work steps: IAS 12.1 Reconcile current tax charge/payable to tax computation or best available tax estimate.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not calculate deferred tax only from P&L movements.

terms.title: IAS 16 - Property, Plant and Equipment
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Recognition, componentisation, measurement, depreciation, revaluation, impairment indicators, disposals and disclosure. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client owns property, plant, equipment, fixtures, vehicles, machinery or assets under construction; Depreciation, revaluation or disposal is material Minimum evidence to obtain: Fixed asset register; Capex invoices; Depreciation policy; Asset lives/residual values; Revaluation reports; Disposal evidence; Physical verification Mandatory work steps: IAS 16.1 Reconcile fixed asset register to trial balance by asset class.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 19 - Employee Benefits
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Short-term employee benefits, bonuses, pensions, defined benefit obligations, termination benefits, actuarial assumptions and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has payroll accruals, bonuses, holiday pay, pension plans, defined benefit schemes, termination programmes or long-service benefits Minimum evidence to obtain: Payroll records; Bonus agreements; Holiday accrual data; Pension scheme documents; Actuarial valuation; Termination plans Mandatory work steps: IAS 19.1 Identify all employee benefit categories and reconcile payroll-related balances to the ledger.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not assume all external schemes are defined contribution.

terms.title: IAS 20 - Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure of government grants and assistance, including conditions and repayment risk. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client receives grants, subsidies, payroll support, asset grants, forgivable loans or other government assistance Minimum evidence to obtain: Grant agreements; Approval letters; Conditions and compliance evidence; Spend schedules; Repayment clauses; Cash receipts Mandatory work steps: IAS 20.1 Create a grant register covering all grants and assistance received or receivable.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 21 - The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Functional currency, foreign currency transactions, foreign operations, translation differences and presentation currency conversion. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has foreign currency transactions, foreign operations, overseas subsidiaries, intercompany balances or group presentation currency conversion Minimum evidence to obtain: Currency of sales/costs/funding; Entity cash flows; Intercompany agreements; Foreign subsidiary trial balances; Exchange rates used; FX reserve movements Mandatory work steps: IAS 21.1 Assess functional currency using primary and secondary indicators.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not use legal country currency by default.

terms.title: IAS 23 - Borrowing Costs
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Capitalisation of borrowing costs for qualifying assets, capitalisation period, eligible costs and suspension or cessation of capitalisation. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client develops or constructs assets taking substantial time to get ready for use or sale; Specific or general borrowings fund qualifying assets Minimum evidence to obtain: Capex project schedules; Loan agreements; Interest schedules; Project timelines; Readiness/use dates; Management approvals Mandatory work steps: IAS 23.1 Identify assets that meet the qualifying asset definition.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not capitalise borrowing costs for routine short-cycle assets.

terms.title: IAS 24 - Related Party Disclosures
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Related party relationships, transactions, balances, commitments, key management compensation and disclosure completeness. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Directors, shareholders, group entities, associates, joint ventures, family members or key management personnel transact with the client Minimum evidence to obtain: Register of directors/shareholders; Group structure; Ledger related-party accounts; Board minutes; Loan agreements; KMP compensation data Mandatory work steps: IAS 24.1 Build a related party register from legal ownership, management enquiry, group structure and board records.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 27 - Separate Financial Statements
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Accounting for investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates in separate financial statements and presentation of separate FS. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Parent, investor or holding company prepares separate financial statements; Investments in subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures exist Minimum evidence to obtain: Investment ledger; Legal ownership documents; Accounting policy; Dividend records; Impairment indicators; Separate FS draft Mandatory work steps: IAS 27.1 Confirm whether the financial statements are separate financial statements and identify investments covered.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 28 - Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Significant influence, equity accounting, impairment and handoff from IFRS 11 joint venture classification. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client owns 20% or more of an investee or otherwise has significant influence; Joint venture classification under IFRS 11 exists Minimum evidence to obtain: Ownership schedule; Board rights; Shareholder agreements; Investee financial statements; Fair value and impairment indicators Mandatory work steps: IAS 28.1 Assess significant influence using voting power, board representation, participation in policy decisions, material transactions and technical information exchange.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 29 - Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Applicability of hyperinflationary accounting, restatement of financial statements and interaction with foreign currency translation. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Entity functional currency is that of a hyperinflationary economy; Foreign subsidiary operates in hyperinflationary jurisdiction; Group consolidation includes hyperinflationary entity Minimum evidence to obtain: Functional currency assessment; Inflation data; General price index; Foreign subsidiary financial statements; Translation schedules Mandatory work steps: IAS 29.1 Screen all entities for hyperinflationary economy indicators.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not rely only on management assertion.

terms.title: IAS 32 - Financial Instruments: Presentation
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Classification of financial instruments as liabilities or equity, compound instruments, offsetting and presentation. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has preference shares, convertible debt, put options, shareholder loans, warrants, derivatives or offsetting arrangements Minimum evidence to obtain: Instrument agreements; Articles/share terms; Settlement terms; Conversion features; Netting agreements; Legal enforceability evidence Mandatory work steps: IAS 32.1 Review contractual substance of each instrument.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not classify based on legal form alone.

terms.title: IAS 33 - Earnings per Share
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Basic and diluted EPS, weighted-average shares, potential ordinary shares and reconciliations for applicable entities. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Entity has publicly traded ordinary shares or is required to present EPS; Potential ordinary shares exist through options, warrants, convertibles or contingently issuable shares Minimum evidence to obtain: Share capital records; Weighted-average share calculation; Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders; Potential ordinary share instruments; Dilution calculations Mandatory work steps: IAS 33.1 Confirm whether IAS 33 applies.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not present EPS unless required or intentionally disclosed with proper basis.

terms.title: IAS 34 - Interim Financial Reporting
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Minimum interim content, condensed financial statements, significant events, accounting policy consistency and disclosures for interim periods. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client prepares interim IFRS financial information; Lender, investor, listing or group requirement asks for interim reporting Minimum evidence to obtain: Interim trial balance; Prior annual financial statements; Significant event log; Seasonality data; Updated estimates; Tax rate estimate Mandatory work steps: IAS 34.1 Confirm whether interim report is full IFRS financial statements or IAS 34 condensed interim reporting.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 36 - Impairment of Assets
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Impairment indicators, CGUs, recoverable amount, value in use, fair value less costs of disposal, assumptions, sensitivities and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Goodwill, indefinite-lived intangibles, impairment indicators, underperforming CGUs, asset damage, market decline or restructuring exists Minimum evidence to obtain: Asset register; CGU structure; Budgets/forecasts; Discount rate support; Market evidence; Impairment indicator assessment; Sensitivity analysis Mandatory work steps: IAS 36.1 Screen for impairment indicators at each reporting date and identify assets requiring annual testing.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not define CGUs to avoid impairment.

terms.title: IAS 37 - Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Recognition and measurement of provisions, contingent liabilities, contingent assets, onerous contracts, restructuring and disclosure. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Legal claims, warranties, onerous contracts, restructuring, restoration obligations, disputes, guarantees or contingencies exist Minimum evidence to obtain: Legal letters; Board minutes; Contracts; Warranty claims data; Restructuring plans; Management estimates; External correspondence Mandatory work steps: IAS 37.1 List all possible obligations and contingencies from legal, board, contract and management sources.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 38 - Intangible Assets
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Recognition and measurement of intangible assets, research and development, software, amortisation, impairment and disclosure. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has software, development projects, licences, brands, customer relationships, websites, patents or internally generated assets Minimum evidence to obtain: Project cost schedules; Development approval; Technical feasibility evidence; Commercial viability evidence; Software invoices; Useful life support Mandatory work steps: IAS 38.1 Identify all intangible asset candidates and reconcile carrying amounts to the ledger.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not capitalise general innovation or exploratory spend.

terms.title: IAS 40 - Investment Property
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Classification, measurement policy, transfers, fair value disclosure and rental income/expense disclosure for investment property. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client holds property to earn rentals or for capital appreciation; Property has mixed owner-occupied and rental use; Transfers between PPE, inventory and investment property occur Minimum evidence to obtain: Property deeds; Lease agreements; Use analysis; Valuation reports; Rental income records; Transfer documentation Mandatory work steps: IAS 40.1 Determine whether property is held to earn rentals, for capital appreciation or owner occupation.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not classify based only on legal ownership.

terms.title: IAS 41 - Agriculture
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Biological assets, agricultural produce at harvest, fair value less costs to sell, transformation and disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has crops, livestock, forestry, vineyards, orchards, fish farming or other biological assets; Agricultural produce is harvested or sold Minimum evidence to obtain: Biological asset register; Physical count or production records; Market price data; Costs to sell; Harvest records; Valuation model Mandatory work steps: IAS 41.1 Identify biological assets and agricultural produce separately.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not account for harvested produce under IAS 41 after harvest; hand off to IAS 2.

terms.title: IAS 1 - Presentation of Financial Statements
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Current presentation standard until IFRS 18 effective date, complete set of financial statements, fair presentation, going concern, classification, offsetting, comparatives and explicit IFRS compliance statement.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Reporting period starts before IFRS 18 is effective; Complete IFRS financial statements are prepared; Going concern, classification, comparative or compliance statement issues exist Minimum evidence to obtain: Current financial statements; Trial balance mapping; Going concern assessment; Comparative statements; Accounting policy notes Mandatory work steps: IAS 1.1 Confirm whether IAS 1 or IFRS 18 applies to the reporting period.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. Do not replace IAS 1 early unless early adoption of IFRS 18 is approved.

terms.title: IFRS 6 - Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Exploration and evaluation expenditure for mineral resources, continuation of prior policies on first-time adoption, impairment trigger variation and IAS 36 measurement handoff. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client operates in mining, oil, gas or mineral exploration; Exploration and evaluation assets are recorded; Technical feasibility or commercial viability is not yet demonstrable Minimum evidence to obtain: Licences and exploration rights; Project cost ledgers; Exploration phase status; Impairment indicators; Management technical reports Mandatory work steps: IFRS 6.1 Screen whether the client has exploration and evaluation activity for mineral resources.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence.

terms.title: IAS 26 - Accounting and Reporting by Retirement Benefit Plans
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Financial statements of retirement benefit plans, especially defined benefit plan net assets and actuarial present value disclosures. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client prepares financial statements for a retirement benefit plan; Engagement covers pension plan financial statements rather than employer pension accounting Minimum evidence to obtain: Plan rules; Plan financial statements; Actuarial report; Plan asset records; Benefit obligation information Mandatory work steps: IAS 26.1 Confirm whether the reporting entity is a retirement benefit plan.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. IAS 26.6 Do not attempt actuarial measurement without specialist support.

terms.title: IAS 39 - Financial Instruments: Recognition and Measurement
terms.definition: Purpose and checklist focus: Limited residual use mainly where an entity elects to continue IAS 39 hedge accounting under IFRS 9 or where specific legacy/exemption circumstances apply. Applicability rule: Apply this section only after confirming the client has transactions, balances, arrangements, disclosures or first-time adoption adjustments that fall within this standard.
terms.example: Applicability triggers: Client has hedge accounting arrangements that may continue under IAS 39; Historical financial instruments accounting references IAS 39; Legacy comparative or transition matter remains open Minimum evidence to obtain: Hedge documentation; Risk management policy; Designation documents; IFRS 9 transition decisions; Derivative confirmations Mandatory work steps: IAS 39.1 Confirm whether IFRS 9 applies and whether IAS 39 is relevant only for permitted hedge accounting continuation or legacy matter.
terms.commonError: Do not mark the standard as not applicable without evidence. IAS 39.2 Do not apply IAS 39 classification and measurement when IFRS 9 requirements apply.

terms.definition: Confirm every Appendix 2 standard has been marked Applicable, Not Applicable, Specialist Screen, or Partner Review Required. Map the quality process from customer specification and production planning to inspection, release, dispatch, complaint handling and corrective action.

terms.howToUse: Escalate product safety, litigation, regulatory, major-customer, recall or material financial exposure immediately.

terms.title: Module 4 - Anti-Fraud & Ethics Controls — Procedure
terms.definition: Perform fraud risk identification by process. Focus on opportunity, pressure, rationalisation indicators and control gaps, but do not make accusations without evidence. terms.example: Assess high-risk transaction areas: supplier creation, bank-detail changes, urgent payments, credit notes, manual journals, stock adjustments, payroll changes and agent commissions. Use red-flag analysis to identify unusual patterns.
terms.commonError: Red flags require follow-up; they do not prove fraud.
terms.howToUse: Document incident protocol and evidence preservation requirements where suspected fraud is raised. Escalate potential fraud, bribery, sanctions match, management override or legal sensitivity before discussing conclusions widely.

terms.title: Module 5 - Audit Readiness & Evidence Management — Procedure

terms.example: Prepare an audit committee or board-level summary where in scope, focusing on material gaps, overdue actions and decisions required.
terms.commonError: Do not submit client evidence that is incomplete, unsupported, inconsistent or unreviewed.
